prs.title: Handle Sonos coordinator moves, session takeovers and announcement clip status
prs.author: mnestrud
prs.merge_state: merge-tree clean on origin/dev d42078eb9; review required, no auto-merge
prs.tldr: _leads_moved_group is now re-checked synchronously after the wait, connection included, so a role given up again is left alone. The flow-load timeout decline holds, because aiosonos create_session can hand back the same session id. Our PROBLEM still stands: a play preparing audio on either player has not bumped cloud_queue_item_generation yet, so the hand-over transfers over it. Checking ATTR_PLAY_ACTION_IN_PROGRESS on both queues fixes it without touching core. Copilot resolved all three threads and has no open issues. Sonos is excluded from auto-approve.
prs.summary: r4333309129: commit 07c354954 moves the readiness predicate into _leads_moved_group (connected, client.player.is_coordinator, group subscribed). _hand_over_moved_group calls it again after _wait_for_moved_group, with no await between that check, the generation/_plays_queue checks and the start of the hand-over. Parametrised tests cover role, status and connection loss, so the fix is verified. r4333309191 (declined): aiosonos 0.1.15 _play_stream_url runs create_session and then load_stream_url, and create_session can return the previously used session id. After a CommandTimeout, the provider cannot tell a timed-out create (old session still active) from a timed-out load into a reused session. Forgetting the queue is the conservative choice. The play command already raised, so the user sees the failure. Decline OK. r4333309171 (declined): holding core playback locks from a provider risks lock-order inversion with transfer_queue's own cmd_ungroup/stop calls, so fixing it in core transfer_queue is the right home. The justification is only half-true, though: core's _transfer_ad_hoc_leadership runs inside cmd_set_members under the old leader's PLAYBACK lock (players/controller.py:1404), and only the new leader is unguarded there. Our PROBLEM is the concrete harm from that gap. Scenario: the user starts a play on either speaker right after the move, and handle_play_action holds the lock and sets ATTR_PLAY_ACTION_IN_PROGRESS while audio prepares. play_media has not run yet, so neither generation has moved. The hand-over then forgets our queue, transfer_queue clears and moves it, and play_index cancels the user's pending play or moves their new items to the other speaker. The suggested patch bails when either queue has the flag set. It is a synchronous check right before the transfer and has been validated: 195 sonos tests pass, and the new test fails without the fix.
blockers: Copilot review on bfd46db85 pending
Your second PROBLEM (hand-over overriding a fresh play) depends on the core transfer_queue lock fix

findings.title: Hand-over overrides a play still preparing audio
findings.detail: cloud_queue_item_generation only moves inside play_media, which runs after the core play action has prepared audio under the queue lock. A user play started on the old or new coordinator in the hand-over window passes every check, then transfer_queue clears/moves the queue and play_index cancels the user's pending play_index or plays the user's new items on the other speaker. Core's own leader hand-over holds the old leader's PLAYBACK lock, so the Sonos path is less guarded than core.
findings.fix: Before forgetting the queue, return when queue.extra_attributes[ATTR_PLAY_ACTION_IN_PROGRESS] is set on either queue_id or new_coordinator.player_id (patch below). The full lock fix stays a core follow-up in transfer_queue.

findings.title: Stream resolution can leave ownership on media never sent to Sonos
findings.detail: _play_stream clears the previous queue and session binding and assigns the incoming _flow_queue_id before awaiting resolve_stream_url, outside the load-settlement try. If resolution fails or is cancelled, Sonos keeps playing the previous queue while MA remembers the replacement with no session. Claude did not flag this.
findings.fix: Resolve the URL before changing queue ownership.

findings.title: Reused session on a flow-load timeout is read as a failed load
findings.detail: GPT Sol rated this a PROBLEM; Claude thinks the decline holds since aiosonos can't tell which step timed out and forgetting the queue is the safe default.
findings.fix: Keep uncertain ownership until reconciled, or have aiosonos expose the load result.

prs.tldr: Small, correct fix. _hass_listener only re-armed the reconnect after a BaseHassClientError, so any other exception out of start_listening() (hass-client 1.3.1 raises an AttributeError on a heartbeat timeout) ended the task and left the HA provider loaded but disconnected until a manual reload. The new test sets an AttributeError on connection_lost and asserts the reload is armed. The upstream root cause is music-assistant/python-hass-client#279. origin/stable has the identical except block at providers/hass/__init__.py:707, so this cherry-picks cleanly. prs.author: balloob

prs.tldr: When a provider can not reach its service at load time (network not up at boot), the loader logged a full traceback and never retried. This PR treats aiohttp.ClientConnectionError as retryable with the normal backoff and logs it as one line unless verbose logging is on. The code change is 5 lines and correct. The new test is broken, so CI is red. The PR body still has a traceback dump, Claude footers and an unticked checklist that the bot flagged.
prs.summary: mass.py change is sound. ClientConnectorError passes through _provider_load_step unchanged because it has a message, so the new isinstance check sees it. It changes the retry contract that until now only retried MusicAssistantError, which is the right call for transient network errors. The test fails for a test-only reason: it uses the mass fixture with _demo_music_provider, but that manifest is not loaded in tests, so get_provider_config raises KeyError and load_provider returns before it ever loads. I confirmed that locally. tests/core/test_provider_load_retry.py already has a _mass_with_load_error helper for exactly this; moving the test there makes it pass (patch below). Copilot's TLS point (ClientSSLError and fingerprint mismatch now retried) is weak: the retry backs off to 120s, and a cert failure at boot is often a wrong clock that fixes itself. Its wrapped-cause point is real but partial: a SetupFailedError raised from an aiohttp error still logs a traceback. That can be a follow-up. The PR description needs the cleanup the bot and Copilot asked for.

prs.tldr: Fixes Roku Media Assistant queue stalls (stale queued slot, false track-change detection, one-shot enqueue) and reports IDLE when the stream freezes at its end. Code looks right and was tested by the author and kees, but it is a draft, Verify fails on unticked checkboxes, and it ships no tests although kees wrote them.
prs.summary: All changes are in the Roku player. play_media and stop now clear the local queued item and reset elapsed tracking, matching the app which drops its queued deeplink on every new deeplink. poll only swaps current media to the queued item when something is queued and the position falls back by more than 10 s, which removes the old abs() check that fired on every fresh play and blanked the current track when nothing was queued. enqueue_next_media retries up to three times, which makes sense since the stream feeder hands the next item over once and marks it enqueued regardless. The end-of-stream detector (PLAYING, position at duration minus 1.5 s, unchanged for 10 s) gives MA the PLAYING to IDLE transition it needs for end-of-queue handling, autoplay and dynamic refill. Note that MA does not advance mid-queue on IDLE, so for a track whose enqueue failed the player now shows IDLE instead of a stuck PLAYING, it does not skip ahead. That is still an improvement. kees verified the behaviour on a current dev nightly and wrote five unit tests that fail on dev and pass with this change. The approach is sound and scoped to the provider. What is left is housekeeping.

prs.summary: The Quick Connect flow itself is reasonable: initiate, poll /QuickConnect/Connect inside external_until with a 10 minute deadline, then trade the secret for a token and store token, user id and device id in setup_data. There are real problems though. (1) The cross-provider constants cleanup is out of scope and broken: audiobookshelf/__init__.py and storytel/__init__.py still import CONF_PASSWORD etc. from their own constants modules, gpodder/setup_flow.py imports names gpodder/__init__ no longer exports, and the audiobookshelf tests fail to collect. The reconfigure finish handler (controllers/config/flows.py:546) merges new values into the stored setup_data, so the pop() calls do nothing. prs.title: Stop a Sendspin player reporting a position ahead of what it is playing
prs.author: caraar12345
prs.merge_state: merge-tree clean on origin/dev d42078eb9; review required, no auto-merge
prs.tldr: Sendspin now recomputes its timeline anchor on every commit, so the reported position and the beat schedule follow aiosendspin's rebase after a producer stall. Pruning keeps unplayed audio for late joiners. maximmaxim345 (Sendspin owner) slimmed it, tested it on hardware and answered every thread. Claude finds it ready (412 tests pass), and Copilot has no open issues. Sendspin is excluded from auto-approval.
prs.summary: I checked the anchor math against aiosendspin 10.2.1 and it holds. _resolve_channel_play_start only shifts _channel_timing forward when the timeline falls behind now + min_send_ahead, and commit_start_us minus produced_audio_us is exact for 100 ms slices at every common rate (tail truncation is under 1 us and only at chunk tails). The join rebases only touch channels without committed audio, so the main channel is unaffected. Each history chunk keeps its own anchor, and the playing-chunk lookup and queued-move lookup use the same boundary (end > now and start > now), so an early timer just reschedules itself. The timer has a per-run uuid task id, call_later debounces it, and the finally block cancels the timer and task after the EOF drain on seek, track change, cancel and close; cancel() awaits the old run before a new one starts. The new pruning cutoff (push clock now minus 1 s) keeps all committed-but-unplayed audio plus 1 s of warm-up for late-join backfill, where the old anchor-based cutoff ran ahead by the initial send-ahead. The beat refresh only fires on moves of 500 ms or more, is guarded against track change and generation bumps, and _flow_track_offset_us now resolves the pass playing now instead of log[-1], which also fixes beats being dropped to the fallback while the producer runs ahead. Maintainer: Yes. maximmaxim345 did not ask the author for changes. He merged dev, slimmed the PR himself (beat refresh now just re-runs _refresh_beat_schedule; first-commit refresh covers a slow source start) and tested it on an ESPHome player and the Sendspin CLI with a forced producer stall. Each of his thread replies points at a fix commit (5d3734d playing-track lookup, 3145a75 cumulative threshold, af833ba repeat pass, d7ca9fae7 per-chunk anchor, d454fe47d drain timer). He deferred two Copilot CRITICALs to a separate PR as dev already has the same behaviour: concurrent beat publishers racing, and analysis vanishing mid-refresh. He also explained pause = stop bumping the metadata generation. All 11 review threads are resolved, CI is SUCCESS, the branch is 0 commits behind origin/dev, labelled bugfix, not draft. reviewDecision is still REVIEW_REQUIRED (no formal approval).
blockers: Your approve (Sendspin is excluded from auto-approval), or leave it to maximmaxim345

findings.title: A sub-500 ms anchor move is not applied during the final drain
findings.detail: _queued_move_start_us_locked only schedules moves of at least 500 ms against the reported anchor, so a smaller rebase followed by no further commit leaves the reported position up to 0.5 s ahead for the buffered tail. GPT Sol rates it a PROBLEM; the threshold is the deliberate design, and the error is bounded.
findings.fix: Apply every queued anchor change on the timer; keep the threshold for beat refreshes only.

findings.title: A third beat publisher at every stream start (race deferred by the maintainer)
findings.detail: on_flow_timeline_changed now fires on the first commit of every run, so it overlaps the play_media metadata publish (sendspin_metadata_*) at each start, on a separate task id. Only the queue-item and generation guards sit after the analysis await, so whichever finishes last wins _last_beat_anchor_us. A stale overwrite needs the metadata path to compute its fallback anchor before the first commit and then have its get_audio_analysis return after the rebase refresh's later call. Both calls are the same single-row aiosqlite query and resolve FIFO, so in practice the order is safe. The maintainer already said he would fix this race for all publishers in a separate PR. That is fine, but it now runs at every play start, not just during retries.
findings.fix: No change in this PR. Track the follow-up, which should serialize the metadata, retry and rebase beat publishers (one task id, or a generation check re-read after the await).

findings.title: flow_track_anchor_us(0) used as a timeline-start getter
findings.detail: _send_beat_schedule now calls playback_session.flow_track_anchor_us(0) to read the raw timeline start and adds the offset itself. The method's docstring describes it as returning the track's file-position-0 anchor, so passing 0 reads oddly.

prs.author: jozefKruszynski
prs.ci: All green on head 018900c6b (lint, test, CodeQL, audit, provider-scope). Locally the dashboard, airplay, milkdrop, chromecast and fully_kiosk suites pass (1190), plus the update_user_profile auth tests.
prs.merge_state: merge-tree clean on origin/dev 0205ecdca (draft, BLOCKED on review)
prs.tldr: Lets the MilkDrop visualizer run on cast dashboards, following the casting user's visualizer_* preferences behind a per-show secret viewer_key. Both last-round Copilot CRITICALs are fixed properly: the key rotates on every show and AirPlay now gets one too. Copilot's new CRITICAL on a mid-launch race does not hold, because viewers re-fetch on the sessions-updated event fired right after commit, so it needs a decline reply. One previously-missed item is real: a repeated self preference change on the same websocket emits no event, so cast viewers get stuck. That is a three-line fix.
prs.summary: The rotation fix is correct. The key is popped before on_show so the consumer's own resolve mints a new one, and on failure the failed key is dropped and the previous one put back, which matches the display still showing the old cast. The API path (no on_show) also gets a fresh key via get_url. The AirPlay change is safe: the tvOS app's LaunchIntent keeps route only to derive player, so extra dashboard_id and viewer_key params are ignored, and the server log still prints only the target origin. Copilot r4234225739 says the new key is valid while _sessions and _session_owners still describe the previous cast. True in the code, but only the display being launched holds the new url, it was already showing that caster, and _signal_sessions_updated right after commit makes the frontend re-fetch viewer_preferences (frontend#2617 subscribes to DASHBOARD_SESSIONS_UPDATED). So the worst case is a sub-second flash of the old caster's preset on the same screen. Decline. Previously missed, auth.py:1608: verified. prs.summary: The architecture discussion is waiting on us. Marcel proposed permanent players plus dynamic API-created temporary players, a better name, and folding in (or replacing) MultiClientStream. OzGav answered on 06-27 with a concrete plan (merge permanent stations now, dynamic mode as a follow-up, 'Web Broadcast' name, multi-value stations entry) and pinged on 07-15. No maintainer reply. prs.title: Fix silent RAOP live-input restarts with a post-start progress anchor
prs.author: devon3000
prs.whats_new: Same head 33ea1bc1f. The critical-gate bot drafted it at 06:33Z because Copilot's zero-instant CRITICAL is still unanswered.
prs.tldr: Some AirPlay 1 receivers stay silent when a Sendspin live input restarts, even though the RAOP transport is fine. A PROGRESS command restores audio, but live inputs often have no metadata, so the existing metadata path never sends one. The PR schedules a PROGRESS anchor 100 ms after every acknowledged RAOP start, with a generation counter so stop, flush or a newer start drop stale anchors. The code is small and the tests pass (212 in test_stream.py). Blockers are the unticked template checklist that fails Verify and two open Copilot threads.
prs.summary: Adds _send_start_progress_anchor to AirPlayStream. On a RAOP route, start() spawns a task that sleeps until the acked audible instant plus 100 ms, takes the metadata lock, checks the generation and connection, and sends PROGRESS=<start_position + elapsed>. stop() and flush() bump the generation. AirPlay 2 starts are unchanged. On normal tracks this does not double up with the post-start media-updated progress, because _last_progress_sent is set and the later push is deduped by the 2 s threshold. Hardware evidence is from the author's local hotfix on a Sonos One SL and an older Klipsch receiver; the generalized patch itself has not been run on them yet.

Delta 62bc5692c review. get_playlist_metadata wraps the provider body in AIArtwork.refreshing(), a per-item_id set of asyncio.Events that is set and removed in a finally. _refresh_playlist (used by the worker's _process and the hourly _refresh_playlists) snapshots those events and waits for them before update_metadata(force_refresh=True).

Deadlocks and waits: the wait happens outside every lock (_refresh_lock is only checked with locked() by refresh(), _store_lock is not held, and the controller's Throttler is entered after the wait). No marked get_playlist_metadata awaits the worker, the hourly pass or their locks. Since the list is a snapshot, a refresh that starts later is never waited for, so the wait cannot starve. A refresh that started after the cover file exists picks the new cover up itself through cover() and _touch, and descriptions through _stored_description. Events are always set, including on cancellation. Unload cancels the worker task at done.wait(). Nothing waits on itself: the worker's own refresh marks only after its wait.

prs.tldr: Out of draft again since 08:52Z and OzGav is re-requested. All 58 review threads are resolved, and the three OzGav points from September (owner_player_id rename, conftest.py removed, deferred import removed) are done in the code. Scope is clean: only the new provider, its tests and en.json keys. Two real bugs remain against the current AudioSource session model. The plugin never calls deselect_source, so a second cast on the same renderer reuses the first cast's cached stream details (with the codec ffmpeg detected), and a DLNA Stop leaves the player showing the DLNA source. Also, any stream teardown during Pause is treated as Stop.
prs.summary: New plugin provider synced from ma-provider-dlna-receiver v1.2.8. It runs one aiohttp UPnP server per MA player (ports from 8298 upward, on one detected IPv4) and one SSDP advertiser per renderer, each with its own UDP 1900 socket (SO_REUSEPORT). Playback goes through play_media with an AUDIO_SOURCE uri, and get_audio_stream proxies the sender's URL. Files touched: only music_assistant/providers/dlna_receiver/*, tests/providers/dlna_receiver/* and 9 new keys in translations/en.json. No core changes. Conventions are mostly fine: get_config_entries is an instance method on dev's model, the registry uses the event bus, tasks go through mass.create_task, and narrow excepts are used. The VERSION file matches other synced providers (yandex_*, kion_music, msx_bridge). The docs URL in the manifest returns 404 until music-assistant.io#626 merges. Unload cancels the metadata task, unsubscribes the player events, sends byebye, closes both UDP transports, stops the aiohttp runner, cancels GENA tasks and leaves mass.http_session open. GPT Sol and I found no leak. Security of the unauthenticated endpoint is reasonable for DLNA: SetAVTransportURI and GENA callbacks are validated against loopback, link-local, multicast and reserved addresses on every redirect hop, redirects are capped at 5, GENA is capped at 32 subs per service with a 1800 s TIMEOUT clamp, and SOAP/DIDL parsing rejects DOCTYPE/ENTITY and anything over 64 KiB. Anyone on the LAN can still play to and set the volume of every exposed player. That is inherent to DLNA and the plugin is opt-in. The remaining issues are about the newer AudioSource session contract. Sessions survive cmd_stop and keep session.streamdetails on re-select (_start_audio_source_session with preserve_details). ffmpeg writes the detected codec into that AudioFormat in place, so the next cast on the same renderer is launched with the old -acodec. Other receivers (airplay_receiver, spotify_connect, ariacast, sendspin_source) call deselect_source with the session's playback_session_id when their session ends. This plugin does not. on_source_unselected also sets STOPPED and clears elapsed on every stream teardown, but dev documents that a paused source's stream can be torn down while the source stays selected.

prs.summary: One new commit, e9350c2 'Send waitingToPlay while the player is buffering' (cli.py: 4 comment lines out, 6 code lines in; the test is parametrized over BUFFERING/BUFFER_READY (flag 1, mode play) and PLAYING/PAUSED/STOPPED (flag absent)). It matches our posted comment and Copilot's medium, which Copilot now lists as resolved. lawrence-jeff replied at 22:35Z that he tried it on a piCorePlayer and a Squeezebox Radio: the flag shows briefly at track start and after a seek. Remaining issue, raised by GPT Sol and confirmed against client.py: _process_stat_stmd promotes the enqueued track via play_url(send_flush=False), which sets state BUFFERING (and STMc sets it again) while the current track keeps playing until STMs. During that window, roughly the output buffer (several seconds), the status now carries waitingToPlay=1, and JiveLite holds its clock, so the display freezes near the end of each track and jumps at the next one. MA's squeezelite provider uses that path in non-flow mode (player.py enqueue=True, send_flush=False). Before this commit the client simply ran its clock there. LMS only sends the flag when nothing is audibly playing. Our own earlier patch had the same gap. Fix: a SlimClient.waiting_to_play property that is True in BUFFERING/BUFFER_READY unless a gapless handoff is in progress (_buffering_media set and no flushed start pending), used by cli.py. I have not seen the freeze on hardware; it follows from the code. Label still missing. After merge: aioslimproto release plus server pin bump (aioslimproto==3.3.0 in music_assistant/providers/squeezelite/manifest.json and requirements_all.txt).

prs.title: Add BookOrbit audiobook music provider
prs.author: justinwoodland
prs.tldr: Three of the five old findings are fixed: the icon, the get_artist forced refresh and the page overlap. The ten-minute JSON timeout and the full refetch on artist refresh are still open. The new unknown-duration progress path writes a complete or reset that the provider can't read back, so a reset in MA can be undone on the next play.
prs.summary: Delta since 9ace49f7a: the BookOrbitAuthError wrapper is replaced by LoginFailed, a shared _reraise_bookorbit_error maps 404/429/HTTP/transport errors to MA errors, TypeError/ValueError from the manifest ordering helper becomes InvalidDataError, grants now survive on_streamed (idle timeout, in-flight transfer count, reusable buffer hold), pagination rejects duplicate ids across pages, progress writes stamp capturedAt before the lock and drop superseded writes after a 409, and single-asset books without a duration send mid-book positions via PUT and complete/reset via the legacy percentage endpoint. The playlog and continue-listening features were added after our last review and fully reverted, with no leftovers. Grant handling matches core: StreamFeeder/AudioBuffer clear streamdetails.buffer and cancelled is a real property, so held grants are bounded by buffer life. Security is fine: part URLs carry only a uuid4 session id scoped to book+assets, the Bearer token goes in a header only, resolve_image only sends credentials to URLs under base_url, and nothing logs a token. Outside providers/bookorbit only translations/en.json changes (the generated keys from strings.json). No requirements changes. The main new issue: for a single asset with unknown duration, a reset (position 0) only goes to legacy /audio-progress. get_resume_position reads playback-state first, which still holds the old mid-book PUT. If playback-state is absent, parse_resume_position still demands every file duration and raises. In both cases the BookOrbit side never reports the reset, and core's 'higher position wins' rule brings the old position back.
blockers: Unknown-duration complete/reset is written where the provider never reads it back, so a reset in MA can come back on the next play
JSON timeout still 10 minutes while catalog and progress locks are held

findings.title: Unknown-duration complete/reset is written where the provider never reads it back
findings.detail: For a single asset without durationMs, mid-book reports PUT playback-state, but fully_played and position 0 return None and go to legacy PATCH /audio-progress only. get_resume_position prefers playback-state whenever it exists, so after a reset it returns the old mid-book positionMs (not completed). Core then takes the higher position (MA 0 vs provider N) and resumes at N, which undoes the reset. When playback-state is absent, parse_resume_position (line 175) still calls _require_known_file_durations and raises ValueError, so the legacy 100% or 0% is never imported either. Other BookOrbit clients that read playback-state also never see the completion. Unless BookOrbit mirrors legacy PATCHes into playback-state (unverified), the new branch only works one way.
findings.fix: For a reset, also PUT playback-state with positionMs=0 so the state matches the legacy write. Drop the upfront _require_known_file_durations in parse_resume_position, because only parts before the current file need a duration and _duration already raises for those. Add a round-trip test: mid-book PUT, then reset, then get_resume_position returns 0.

findings.title: JSON requests still allow ten minutes while catalog/progress locks are held
findings.detail: AIOHTTP_TIMEOUT is still ClientTimeout(total=600, sock_connect=60) with no sock_read. A BookOrbit server that accepts the connection and then stalls holds _catalog_lock (blocking browse/search/get_artist) or a per-book progress lock for up to ten minutes per request. Unchanged since the last round.
findings.fix: Use a short JSON timeout, e.g. ClientTimeout(total=60, sock_connect=15, sock_read=30). Large transfers already use PART_STREAM_TIMEOUT.

findings.title: Refreshing one artist still refetches every book detail and manifest
findings.detail: get_artist now forces only under BYPASS_CACHE, which fixes the old problem. But under music/refresh_item BYPASS_CACHE also bypasses the non-persistent CACHE_CATEGORY_BOOK entries in _get_book_detail, so one artist refresh runs GET /books/{id} plus a manifest for every multipart book in all libraries.
findings.fix: Refresh only the catalog card lists and author list for an artist refresh, and keep using checksum-matched book cache (pass allow_bypass=False on the book cache get, since updatedAt already invalidates it).

findings.title: Title-only sort plus the new duplicate-id rejection can fail sync on title ties
findings.detail: The query sorts by title only. With LIMIT/OFFSET paging, rows that share a title have no guaranteed order between pages (Postgres top-N sorts are known for this). Before, that meant a silent duplicate or skip. Now a duplicate raises BookOrbitIncompleteError, so the whole catalog refresh fails, and it can keep failing for libraries with repeated titles across a 100-item page boundary.
findings.fix: Add a unique tiebreaker: "sort": [{"field": "title", "dir": "asc"}, {"field": "id", "dir": "asc"}] (if BookOrbit accepts multi-key sort), or sort by id alone since order does not matter for a sync.

findings.title: Unknown-duration legacy updates can't round-trip
findings.detail: The new branch writes single-file completion or reset without a duration, but parse_resume_position() still requires every file duration, so reading it back raises ValueError and the provider falls back to MA's position.

findings.title: JSON requests still hold locks for ten minutes
findings.detail: AIOHTTP_TIMEOUT stays total=600 with no read timeout, so a stalled server blocks catalog refresh and per-book progress sync while their locks are held.

prs.title: Let an application add its own routes to the CLI web server
prs.author: lawrence-jeff
prs.ci: green (lint, test 3.11). PR Labels check has not run yet and the PR has no label; it needs new-feature.
prs.tldr: Adds an optional extra_routes {path: handler} dict to SlimServer so an app can serve artwork and icons on the CLI web port. Small, additive, tested. Author asks for a design opinion; the hook is the right shape.
prs.summary:
SqueezePlay/JiveLite clients fetch artwork for cover ids (/music/<id>/cover_WxH_m.png), relative icon paths (html/images/*.png) and remote images (/imageproxy/...) from the web server they do JSON-RPC against, which is the aiohttp app aioslimproto owns on cli_port_json. Today nothing answers those paths. The PR lets the app pass in aiohttp routes at construction, registered with method * after /jsonrpc.js and /cometd. Default behavior unchanged. Tests start a real CLI web server and pass locally (4 passed).

Design opinion for Marvin: approve the approach. The serving logic needs MA library and image proxy access, so it belongs in the provider, and the library cannot add routes after start because aiohttp freezes the router. A constructor dict is the simplest API that works and survives stop/start (the app is rebuilt each start and the dict is replayed). Alternatives are not clearly better: a RouteDef list adds method control nobody needs yet, a setup callback leaks the web.Application, and a public add_route still has to buffer until start. Emitting absolute URLs to MA's own web server would cover menu items the provider builds, but not the paths clients generate themselves from a coverid/icon-id (sized /music/<id>/cover_* variants, imageproxy requests, client-side html/images assets), so the hook is still needed.

Points to raise with the author: the docstring's ordering claim is only accurate for aiohttp 3.9 linear matching; 3.10+ resolves by path-prefix buckets (verified in aiohttp 3.13.5). The provider side should match sized cover paths (cover_225x225_m.png style), not only /music/{id}/cover, and the explicit 404 catch-all is redundant since aiohttp already 404s. Merging needs an aioslimproto release plus a server pin bump (server origin/dev pins 3.3.0), and the server provider does not pass cli_command_handler or extra_routes yet; the author's provider rework is not in a server PR yet.

prs.title: Don't blame the address when a self-hosted speech server is slow to start
prs.author: marcelveldt
prs.tldr: OpenAI TTS setup now gives a slow self-hosted server 120 s to render the test phrase (10 s connect cap) and reports a slow render as render_timeout instead of cannot_connect. Clean, Copilot approves, CI green.
prs.summary: The setup test render used a 30 s total timeout and mapped every ClientError or TimeoutError to 'Could not reach the speech API'. Self-hosted servers that load the model on the first request (mlx-audio, LocalAI, Speaches) can take longer, so a valid address was blamed. Now the validation timeout is ClientTimeout(total=SPEECH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=120, connect=10). ConnectionTimeoutError is a ClientError, so an unreachable host still fails as cannot_connect within 10 s; a plain TimeoutError (total timeout while waiting for headers or reading the body) becomes the new render_timeout error with the seconds as arg. Checked against aiohttp 3.14.3 source: the total timeout raises plain asyncio.TimeoutError in both phases, no sock_read timeout is set, and the except order is correct. Going past the flow engine's 120 s NEXT_STEP_TIMEOUT (voices lookup 10 s + render 120 s) is handled by the existing 'working' progress step. The test covers both mappings and asserts the timeout passed to the request. Not runnable locally (shared .venv has stale models, ListingType import error); CI pytest is green.

prs.title: Party: add configurable number of votes required to skip a song
prs.author: martinbuergi
prs.tldr: The rework is what you asked for: votes on the queue item, no plugin state, listener or cleanup, 33/33 tests. All three reviewers hit the same gap: the tally is popped before next() takes the strict playback lock, so votes queued behind that lock can skip a second, unvoted song. Copilot also flags stale tallies on replayed items.
prs.summary:
Head e510bea55 (merge-base 44bd993bc) does what Marvin asked on 10-28. The voters are a comma-joined string in extra_attributes['party_skip_voters'] with the count in 'party_skip_votes'. _on_queue_updated, _remove_stale_skip_tally, _clear_skip_votes, _has_next_track, the skip locks and the plugin vote fields are all gone (grep finds no leftover QUEUE_UPDATED subscription or vote state). The has_player_access gate and the optional queue_item_id stay. song_changed is returned when the guest's item is no longer current.

Atomicity: _get_voter_id is the only await before the read, and the read, add, write and signal_update(items_changed=True) are all synchronous. On the threshold both keys are popped and signal_update runs before 'await next()'. Uncontended, next() moves queue.current_item synchronously: the lock acquire does not yield and the item is set before call_later(play_index). So a concurrent vote gets song_changed. Contended, next() first waits on get_group_and_player_lock(strict=True), for example while the debounced play_index of an earlier skip, or a host or party play action, holds it. current_item stays on the old item for that time, so votes naming the old item still count on an empty ledger, and reaching the threshold again queues a second next(). test_skip_votes_are_dropped_before_skipping encodes this 'starts over' behaviour.

Persistence: queue.current_item is the same object as in queue_data.items (get_item, update_items keep the references). QueueItem.to_cache keeps extra_attributes, and items_cache_dirty causes the debounced items write, so the votes survive a restart or reload.

Double voting: the same token twice is deduped. Rejoining still mints a new token_id, because the join code can be reused until it expires and exchange_join_code only rate-limits failures, so a second vote from the same person counts. This is the best per-device identity available. The guest already has QUEUES_CONTROL plus player access, so it could call player_queues/next directly, and skip rate limiting is client-side, so the threshold is a UX control, not enforcement.

Threshold change: votes_required is read on every vote. Lowering it does not act on an existing tally until the next request, and then even a duplicate (uncounted) vote skips, because 'skipped' does not depend on vote_counted.

Same song later: a re-request is a new QueueItem with a new queue_item_id, so it starts at zero. But a partial tally on an item that played to the end stays on that item and comes back if that same QueueItem is replayed (previous, Repeat All wrap, play_index on history). That contradicts the string 'Votes reset when the next song starts'.

Last track with repeat off: the votes are dropped and next() does nothing, so the response says skipped=True and the frontend shows 'Song skipped!'. Marvin accepted this. The frontend resets its voted state when the tally drops to 0, so guests can vote again.

Frontend#3014 (head 4a25ff31) sends queue_item_id, and handles song_changed, vote_counted, skipped, votes and votes_required. It reads party_skip_votes from current_item and shows the tally only for position=current, and it has already dropped no_next_track, so the contract matches. Dev drift since the merge-base (auth_middleware impersonation scope, transfer_queue) does not touch this path.
blockers: Fix: take get_group_and_player_lock(queue_id, strict=True) before reading and popping the tally

prs.tldr: The play_index fast path now keys on source_current_item, captured before the source is stopped, and only fires if that item still exists in the target. prs.summary: Delta 3073fb3ab..b22cc7e1d replaces target_queue.current_item with source_current_item in the auto_play guard. Previously update_items could resync the target's current_item to a replacement item, which then passed the index_by_id check and got play_index at the missing item's offset. Now a missing source item fails the guard, and the elif auto_play path calls resume(). Two sub-cases. When the target has a buffered index, update_items calls _resync_position, which sets resume_pos=0 and elapsed_time=0. resume() then computes resume_pos = 0 or _last_played_position() = 0, because the target's prev_state names a different queue_item_id. When the target has no buffered index, resume() sees the parked item missing and takes its explicit 'no valid current item' branch with resume_pos=0. Radio and ended handling are unchanged. The new test covers the buffered-index case and asserts play_index is not awaited and resume_pos is 0.

prs.author: OzGav
prs.merge_state: merge-tree clean on origin/dev d42078eb9; review required, no auto-merge
prs.tldr: get_url_data now deletes the 30-day settled entry when a lookup finds the URL unknown or ambiguous. Keys match the set call and cache.get honours BYPASS_CACHE, so a refresh really re-asks and clears it. The declined CRITICAL needs three rare conditions at once, and the harm is a duplicate rather than a wrong merge. Ready. Copilot recommends approval on the head. Core touched, so it's your approve.
prs.summary: Delta 80c73af04..3ac44a43d adds an else branch in MusicBrainzAPIClient.get_url_data that calls mass.cache.delete(settled_key, provider=self.domain) whenever the lookup does not resolve to exactly one entity. The key and provider are the same as in the set call. delete() with category None matches any category, and set uses the default 0, so the entry is removed. cache.get_with_freshness returns a miss under BYPASS_CACHE for non-persistent entries, so a bypassing refresh skips the settled entry, re-queries and now drops it. That closes r4337198057. Concurrent lookups for one URL are last-writer-wins, and both writers reflect MusicBrainz at their own time, so no harmful race. A 400/401/404 response (None) also drops the settled entry, which is right for 404 and harmless otherwise because the 1-day cache re-asks. The new test drives the real set/delete sequence with BYPASS_CACHE. On the declined r4337197972: the recovered MBID is only applied at insert, after _get_library_item_by_match has run its external-id pass without it. A duplicate therefore needs a same-provider name clash, a MusicBrainz URL link, and a third library artist carrying that MBID under a name that normalises differently (localised names, P!nk/Pink). OzGav's premise that library artists carry the MusicBrainz name is not quite right: names come from the first provider. Even so the combination is rare, and the outcome (a duplicate with the same MBID, mergeable by hand) is better than the pre-PR behaviour, which merged the item into the wrong same-name artist. Decline accepted. A cheap follow-up would look up the recovered MBID before inserting.

prs.title: Keep a track's length after its queue moves to another player
prs.author: Simanias
prs.merge_state: merge-tree clean on origin/dev d42078eb9; review required, no auto-merge
prs.tldr: Stops _cleanup_queue_audio_data (and the stale sweep) set streamdetails.buffer to None before clear(), so the writeback took the cut-off stream for a clean source and shortened the track. The PR keeps the buffer reference from the first chunk in both the single-item and the flow path. Radio and unbuffered sources fall back to the old check unchanged. Both new cases fail on dev and pass here.
prs.summary: Every release path detaches before clearing: stream_feeder _cleanup_queue_audio_data, the stale-buffer sweep, the prepare_next orphan, and get_audio_buffer's invalid-buffer reuse. AudioBuffer.clear() always sets _cancelled. The old writeback read streamdetails.buffer after the stream ended, found None, and wrote the truncated stream length as the item's duration, for example when a queue is transferred to another player. Now source_buffer is the buffer of the first chunk (a capacity reselection happens before the first yield, so that is the buffer the item really plays from), with streamdetails.buffer as fallback. Other paths: radio, realtime and unbuffered items have no buffer and behave as before. Flow mode resets source_buffer per track inside the loop. The crossfade tail accounting is unchanged. A consumer that leaves (GeneratorExit) never reaches the writeback. get_media_stream's producer-side writeback only runs when the stream finished. Players that report their own duration do not go through this code. The one theoretical change: a fully played buffer that gets cleared before the writeback runs now keeps the provider's duration instead of the measured one. That is harmless. On tests: the flow test gains a released_by_stop case, a new single-path test was added, and an existing SimpleNamespace fixture got buffer=None so the first-chunk read works; no assertion got weaker. Both new cases fail against origin/dev audio.py. Ruff and mypy are clean.

prs.title: Let a player ask for a larger lead on the flow stream
prs.author: Simanias
prs.merge_state: merge-tree clean on origin/dev 04434955a; review required, no auto-merge
prs.tldr: Opt-in per-player setting that serves the flow stream at the pre-#6584 pace (1.03x, 3 s burst). It is on by default for Raumfeld, whose renderers otherwise re-request /flow/ at a track end. Simanias fixed both Copilot findings: requires_reload, and forced_content_length streams keep the usual pace because only they get the 8 s lead-out. Claude and GPT Sol verified it; Copilot recommends approval. It touches core streams code, so it is your or Marcel's approve.
prs.summary: The PR adds a FLOW_LEAD pacing profile (1.03x, 3 s burst) and a per-player advanced boolean that the flow route reads from the requesting protocol player, with Raumfeld defaulting it on. Entry injection in _get_player_config_entries is correct (HTTP-based players that support PLAY_MEDIA), and the Raumfeld override uses the same from_dict default-override pattern as flow mode, so the provider entry replaces the generic one. The Copilot PROBLEM is valid: without requires_reload the toggle has no effect on an active flow until the next stream, unlike its flow-mode siblings. In a sync group the leader's setting applies, which is consistent with other per-player stream settings, but universal groups ignore it because the UGP runner hardcodes NEAR_REALTIME. Tests pass and the change is small (36 code lines). Architecture: A per-player opt-in is a reasonable, low-risk stopgap: it is off by default, it reuses the existing pacing-profile seam, and it leaves the #6584 Chromecast rationale intact for everyone else. The real flaw is central and already on dev: since #6608, _get_flow_start_item resumes a re-requested /flow/ at the current item but from its start, so the track replays. Resuming at the elapsed position (or answering a late re-request with the next item) would fix every renderer that reconnects without a per-device knob, so this should be framed as a mitigation until Marcel decides on that. Tests: 246 passed (streams + raumfeld), 27 passed (config entry tests), ruff clean.

The pace is fixed when the /flow/ ffmpeg process starts, so toggling the setting mid-play changes nothing until the next stream. A user who turns it on because the queue starts over will see it happen again at the next track end and conclude it does not work. prs.title: Keep the library when a migration runs out of disk space
prs.author: MarvinSchenkel
prs.merge_state: merge-tree clean on origin/dev 5fe304524; review required, no auto-merge
prs.tldr: The slimmed PR fixes the reported wipe: cache.clear() no longer runs under the migration catch-all, and the skipped analysis move retries on every start while the legacy tables remain. Claude finds it ready (1599 music tests pass; the 3 new tests hang on dev), and Copilot recommends approval. Any other disk-full error during a migration still wipes library.db, as on dev. Claude and GPT Sol suggest a follow-up or a narrower title.
prs.summary: The reported failure is fixed: cache.clear() no longer runs under the migration catch-all, and the skipped analysis move is retried, inside migrate_database for any migration and at startup when the stored version is current. The retry is gated on the legacy tables still being in sqlite_master, which costs two lookups per start once they are gone. It is idempotent after a partial move: rows go in batches with ON CONFLICT newer-wins, completeness is verified by natural key, and the source is dropped only when complete. The free-space math is consistent (bytes / 2^30 on both sides, measured on storage_path where both db files live) and conservative, because the packed destination is smaller than the JSON source. There is no lock race with audio_analysis.db, since the streams controller only opens it in post_setup, after the music setup is done. DB_SCHEMA_VERSION is 71 on both the PR and origin/dev. prs.title: Keep a Universal Player's id when a stale native player claims its protocol
prs.author: MarvinSchenkel
prs.merge_state: merge-tree clean on origin/dev d42078eb9; review required, no auto-merge
prs.tldr: A Universal Player now keeps its id across restarts: the startup handover to a stale native config is gone, and a native only takes over the wrapper when it actually registers, through the refuse-aware runtime transfer with the #6610 same-domain guard. Claude finds it ready: 771 tests pass, and 4 of the 5 new tests fail on dev. Copilot recommends approval. GPT Sol notes a partial claim takes the whole wrapper, which you already argued in the Copilot thread.
prs.summary: Checked each behaviour change against the code. The startup handover is gone and _restore_player always registers the UP. _check_replace_universal_player gains a config-claim gate: the registering native's linked_protocol_ids must intersect the UP's known protocols, and the same-domain guard must not fire. Past that gate it reuses the existing runtime transfer, so refused groups stay on the UP, only moved ids migrate when something is refused, and the UP is removed only when nothing is refused. Unregistered UP protocols migrate in config to the native and recover through the cached parent, so no protocol ends up orphaned or owned twice. Registration order is covered both ways: natives that register after the restore go through _try_link_protocols_to_native, and natives that registered earlier are rechecked by the loop at the end of discover_players. Disabled natives never register (controller.register returns early), so they can't take a UP. Enabling one later triggers the claim path, which matches the PR body. The guard reads persisted protocol_parent_id, so it works before the native's own output has registered, and it behaves like the removed provider guard (same domain set, same exclusions). Nothing else references _reparent_protocols_to_native or the provider-side _owns_domain_of_protocols, no migration or README depends on the startup handover, and dev has not touched these files since the merge-base. The deleted restore tests are either covered by existing runtime tests (config carry-over, native name/DSP/queue precedence, plus the new purge_saved_queue assertion) or were dropped on purpose (cascade-disable and the single-wrapper two-claimer case, both removed behaviour argued in the Copilot thread). prs.title: Resume WiiM playback after the firmware restarts the stream on the first group join
prs.author: MarvinSchenkel
prs.merge_state: merge-tree clean on origin/dev 04434955a; review required, no auto-merge
prs.tldr: After the first follower joins a playing 24-bit WiiM leader, the provider detects the firmware's stream restart and seeks back to where it was (hardware-verified). Claude and GPT Sol agree your decline of Copilot's pause CRITICAL holds, since it is the same core seek path as on dev. Both found one gap: a Next/Previous queued behind the join, or a natural track change, gets the old position applied to the new item. A queue-item check fixes it (validated patch, 237 tests).
prs.summary: Detection is narrow: it arms only for the first follower of a PLAYING leader on a seekable MA queue, and fires only on TRANSITIONING for the pre-join URI within the join plus 2 s. Second followers, removes, paused leaders, live streams and external sources are excluded. Lock handling is sound: the playback locks are task-reentrant, the wait does not take a lock, and the deferred seek takes the group lock before the player lock like any play action, so there is no deadlock or inversion. The pause-during-preparation decline is justified because it is the same play_index path as a user seek on dev. The remaining gap: a Next or Previous queued behind the join moves the queue without calling any WiiM method, so the deferred seek applies the old position to the new item. A one-check item-id guard (patch validated) fixes this and also covers a natural track change reported as TRANSITIONING before the URI updates. Decline: Correct. Once _seek_after_join_restart passes its check it calls player_queues.seek, the same play_index -> _load_item -> play_media path a user seek takes on dev. queue.pause takes no playback lock there either and does not cancel an in-flight play_index, so a pause during stream preparation is undone on dev for every user seek too. The provider path does not widen that window: the check and the seek's reentrant lock run back to back with no await between them, and the earlier windows (during the join, during the 2 s wait, while waiting for the lock) are covered by _drop_join_restart_resume. One caveat: 'well under a second' does not hold when _load_item has to refetch expired streamdetails, but that applies to user seeks just the same.

Needs another maintainer's approval (your own PR)

findings.title: A queued Next/Previous or natural track change gets the old position applied
findings.detail: player_queues.next/previous are play actions, so a Next pressed during the join waits for the leader's playback lock behind cmd_set_members. It is queued before the resume task exists, so it gets the lock first. It sets current_index to the next item and schedules play_index via call_later(1). No WiimPlayer method runs, so _pending_join_resume survives. The resume task then gets the lock, passes the pending check and calls seek(queue_id, position). seek validates against the new current item and calls play_index(new_index, seek_position=position), and play_index cancels the debounced timer (queue_play_index_*). Result: the next track starts at the previous track's position, or the seek fails with InvalidCommand if the new track is shorter. For Previous with more than 5 s elapsed, the restart-to-0 is undone. The same guard also covers a natural track change that reports TRANSITIONING before the new metadata arrives (current_media.uri comes from AVTransportURIMetaData/CurrentTrackMetaData, which the SDK only replaces when present). Not on dev, since the deferred seek is new. This partly reopens Copilot thread 4348826111: that decline argued the device never advances its URI, which still holds, but deferring the seek opened a path where the queue moves without the device. GPT Sol found the same from the track-boundary side: the SDK keeps the outgoing URI until new metadata arrives.
findings.fix: Store current_item.queue_item_id in the watch, and under the locks skip the seek if get_active_queue(self) is no longer that queue or that item. See patch (adds one test, existing tests untouched).

findings.title: Every first-follower join of a playing leader holds the playback lock 2 s longer
findings.detail: The watch arms regardless of the stream's bit depth, and _resume_after_join_restart runs in the finally while cmd_set_members still holds the leader's PLAYBACK lock. A join that never restarts (16-bit streams, most sources) therefore delays set_members by JOIN_RESTART_TIMEOUT and makes play/next/seek/stop on the leader wait for it. This is not a correctness problem, and the held lock is what lets queued commands drop the resume, so it is a reasonable trade-off.
findings.fix: Either accept and mention it in the PR body, or gate _create_join_restart_watch on the current stream's output bit depth if the provider can read it cheaply. No change required.

findings.detail: The helper mocks get_group_and_player_lock() and seek(), so lock contention and ordering are not exercised.

prs.title: Auto pair Sendspin clients through Home Assistant
prs.author: arturpragacz
prs.merge_state: merge-tree clean on origin/dev d42078eb9; review required, no auto-merge
prs.tldr: Solid, well-tested auto-pair. Security holds: admin-gated on the HA side, token client_id checked, PSK never sent or logged. Two calls for Marvin: accept Sendspin->hass by-name coupling (extends the #4916 esphome-enrichment precedent, no depends_on) or ask for a core capability; and MA 'Unpair' gets undone immediately for HA-adopted devices.
prs.summary: HA follows the Sendspin client ids of ESPHome devices and hands out their pairing token over two admin websocket commands (core#188351). Sendspin pairs an announced, connected, encrypted, unpaired client with that token through the existing pair_with_token path. Lifecycle handling is careful: background subscribe, a generation guard, one attempt per client with one follow-up, cancellation on unload. Copilot's earlier lifecycle findings are fixed. Who can pair: no MA user or API action is involved and no new MA API command is added. The trigger is an HA announcement of a client that is connected to MA, encrypted, unpaired (not LONG_TERM with a record), not in a running manual PIN session, and offers PAIRING_PSK. Trust chain: the HA token configured in the hass provider must be admin (both core commands are require_admin), and the device must be adopted in HA's ESPHome integration, which is admin-gated too. What is trusted from HA: the client-id list (only a trigger, filtered locally) and the token. pair_with_token decodes it, requires token.client_id == the connected client_id, and runs the PAIRING_PSK handshake. A wrong or malicious token fails the handshake and is not trusted. Pairing is standalone (owner=None), the same as the settings-flow token paste. Token handling: fetched fresh per attempt, never stored. It is not logged: the error paths log only the exception, and the hass_client 'Received message' debug log is suppressed because the hass provider forces that logger to its own level + 10. It does travel over the HA websocket, which is plaintext ws when HA is configured as http://. That is no worse than HA's own ESPHome API link to the device. Failure modes: HA not loaded: _hass returns None, no subscription, manual pairing unchanged. HA loads later: PROVIDERS_UPDATED snapshot change -> subscribe. HA connection drop: the hass provider reloads via unload+load, both signal PROVIDERS_UPDATED, so the pairer unsubscribes and then resubscribes. Old HA without the commands, or a non-admin token: FailedCommand -> None with a debug log, so the feature degrades silently. HA going away mid-attempt: the token lookup returns None. Sendspin not loaded: the new HA methods are never called. Sendspin unload: close() cancels running attempts, and a subscription answered after teardown is dropped through the generation counter. Subscribing runs in a background task, so HA never blocks Sendspin startup. Open points: the HA/Sendspin coupling (rule says no; precedent from #4916 says it already exists), unpair being undone automatically, and no retry for a transient no-token while the client stays announced. Coupling: Soft, optional, one-way-by-lookup but two-way-by-naming coupling. No manifest depends_on was added (sendspin/manifest.json has none; Sendspin runs fine without HA). Imports: sendspin/hass_auto_pair.py imports HomeAssistantProvider only under TYPE_CHECKING; no runtime import of the hass package. Lookup: HassAutoPairer._hass does cast(HomeAssistantProvider, mass.get_provider("hass")) by domain name (hass_auto_pair.py:77). Direct calls: Sendspin calls two new Sendspin-specific methods on the concrete HA provider, hass.subscribe_sendspin_clients() and hass.get_sendspin_pairing_token() (hass/__init__.py:532-569), which wrap the HA websocket commands sendspin/subscribe_clients and sendspin/get_pairing_token from home-assistant/core#188351. Lifecycle: provider.py hooks subscribe/unsubscribe onto the existing PROVIDERS_UPDATED hass-availability snapshot (provider.py:499, 1944-1947) and close() into unload. So the HA provider now carries a Sendspin-specific API and Sendspin names the HA provider. Against the rule: no depends_on chain, so that part holds. It does break the stricter wording from OzGav on #4576 (providers must never reference each other by name). It is not new to Sendspin, though. dev already has the same pattern for ESPHome announce enrichment from #4916: sendspin/provider.py:1240 and sendspin/player.py:1438 call get_provider("hass").get_media_player_device_infos(). Core code does the same in webserver/remote_access and auth_providers. So the PR widens an existing, accepted seam rather than opening a new one. The rule-clean version is a core-owned capability, e.g. a pairing-token source registry on the players controller that hass registers into, but there is exactly one implementer (ESPHome via HA). This is a maintainer call: accept it as an extension of the #4916 precedent, or ask for the capability now. Blocking on it alone seems heavy-handed.
prs.whats_new: Merged by you at 08:15Z.
blockers: Your call: accept Sendspin looking up the HA provider by name (extends the #4916 precedent, no depends_on) or ask for a core capability
Unpairing an HA-announced device in MA is undone right away (f2)

findings.title: Sendspin looks up the HA provider by name and calls Sendspin-specific methods on it
findings.detail: get_provider("hass") plus subscribe_sendspin_clients/get_sendspin_pairing_token couples the two providers both ways (HA now exposes a Sendspin API, Sendspin names HA). This goes against the provider-isolation rule from #4576. Mitigations: no depends_on, TYPE_CHECKING-only import, optional at runtime, and the same pattern already exists on dev for ESPHome enrichment (#4916, provider.py:1240, player.py:1438).
findings.fix: Maintainer decision. Either accept it as an extension of the #4916 seam, ideally by moving the existing enrichment lookup and this pairer behind one small hass-bridge module so there is a single place that touches HA, or ask for a core-owned pairing-token capability that hass registers and Sendspin queries without naming hass.

findings.title: Unpairing an HA-announced device in MA is undone right away
findings.detail: unpair_client -> server_api.unpair closes a long-term session. The device reconnects as Sentinel, ClientConnectedEvent fires, and on_client_connected re-pairs it with a fresh token from HA (HA fetches it from the device on demand, core#188351). The user cannot keep an HA-adopted device unpaired (for example to use trusted-unpaired mode or hand it to another server), and the feature has no opt-out toggle.
findings.fix: Ask the author whether this is intended. If not: skip clients the user explicitly unpaired, or add a single provider toggle 'Pair Home Assistant devices automatically' (default on).

findings.title: A failed token fetch is not retried while the client stays announced and connected
findings.detail: _on_clients only triggers ids that were not in the previous snapshot. If get_sendspin_pairing_token returns None (device API error, not ready), the client stays unpaired until it reconnects to MA or drops out of the HA list and comes back. The test docstring in test_no_token_leaves_the_client_for_the_next_announcement says 'the next snapshot from Home Assistant asks again', which the code does not do for an id that stays listed. Copilot raised the same gap.
findings.fix: Either correct the docstring, or retry every announced id on each snapshot. _needs_pairing filters paired and disconnected clients locally before any HA call, so this is cheap. See the patch; test_newly_announced_clients_are_paired asserts the current new-ids-only behaviour and would need the author to update it.

findings.title: A rejected token loops on every reconnect
findings.detail: If the device rejects the PSK (HandshakeAbortedError), the server drops the connection. The client reconnects and on_client_connected starts another attempt with a fresh device round-trip through HA and another warning. A legitimate device should not hit this, since the token is fresh. A client that impersonates an announced client_id would, but it cannot learn the PSK: the token is used as the Noise PSK and is never sent, and pair_with_token checks token.client_id against the connection.
findings.fix: Optional: after a failed attempt, log at debug level and skip the client until the next snapshot that changes it.

prs.title: Let the sleep timer stop at the end of the current item or chapter
prs.author: fmunkes
prs.waiting_on: you: approve + release models#448, confirm the design
prs.tldr: The rework does what Marvin asked: the queue owns the target, stops on the per-second position check, and expires_at is only a UI estimate. Two gaps remain. An announcement on a standalone player goes through _handle_stop and silently drops the item/chapter timer before playback resumes, and an END_OF_ITEM stop still cuts early when the real audio runs longer than the metadata duration. CI is red only because models#448 is not released.
prs.summary: c177921bec moves the END_OF_ITEM/END_OF_CHAPTER target onto PlayerQueueData as a SleepTimerTarget (mode, queue_item_id, stop_position). PlaybackTrackerMixin._handle_sleep_timer runs on every queue update. _poll_players triggers one per second for every playing player through a 0.5 s debounce, so players that report rarely are still covered through corrected_elapsed_time. It stops when the target item reaches stop_position, and it also stops when the item changes or restarts within 5 s of the stop (enqueue-ahead players and device repeat). Any other item change re-pins, as a device skip. On IDLE it stops, and when the queue goes inactive it clears. _get_next_index returns None for the target on a natural advance (is_skip still moves on), which also covers repeat-one, crossfade and the flow stream. play_index re-pins on every MA next/previous/seek/resume and now also refreshes playback_speed. _handle_stop and mark_ended clear the target, as asked (this covers the 30 s pause auto-stop). _stop_for_sleep_timer clears first so next_item comes back, and _handle_end_of_queue then sees a mid-queue stop instead of the end of the queue. The flow stream that ends through the gate is torn down by the _handle_stop session clear before _resume_on_idle's 1 s + 1 s check. The players controller keeps the API, the duration call_later and sleep_timer_mode. update_sleep_timer_expires_at only publishes the estimate, with a 1 s jitter guard. prs.title: Follow artists and albums MusicBrainz merged into others
prs.author: OzGav
prs.tldr: Ready, core: when MusicBrainz merges an artist or release, the stored MusicBrainz id is swapped for the new one (only that id, re-read first) and an artist is joined with the library artist that already holds the new id via the existing merge path. Ids from a name search are not followed in that run. 279 tests pass. Costs one or two extra MusicBrainz requests per merged item, once; OzGav accepts that. Remaining points are suggestions.
prs.summary: The PR swaps a stored MusicBrainz artist id (MB_ARTIST) or release id (MB_ALBUM) for the id MusicBrainz now answers with after a merge. It joins a followed artist with library artists that already hold the new id, and it skips following for an id a name search found in the same run. The swap (_store_musicbrainz_id) re-reads the stored external ids and only replaces the MusicBrainz tuple. That works because MB_* ids are unique in add_external_id, so the in-memory set loses exactly the id the getter returned and other ids, a second MB_ARTIST included, are kept. The later update_item_in_library unions db and in-memory ids, both of which now hold only the new id, so the old one is not written back. The read/write window has no lock, but neither does dev's own _update_library_item. Both artist entry points (link_item_to_musicbrainz and _update_artist_metadata) handle the join. merge_library_artists_by_mbid / merge_library_items already exist on dev and move provider mappings, favourites, playlog, genres, references and album/track artist relations, keeping the oldest row and merging only artists of the same artist_type. MusicBrainz merges are duplicates by definition, so a correct stored id cannot join two different artists. Album semantics are right: MB_ALBUM is the release id, resolve_release tries it first, and a release that differs because the stored id 404s on the mirror is kept, since the cached None makes get_release_details raise InvalidDataError. Release groups (MB_RELEASEGROUP) are not followed, and albums are not joined. Neither is a regression. A reliably found new id is already canonical, because identify_artist returns details.id. Rate limiting on dev is ThrottlerManager(30, 10) against musicbrainz-mirror.music-assistant.io, not 1 req/s, and every extra request goes through it. I checked every finding against origin/dev; the touched areas have no drift since the merge base.

prs.author: dmoo500
prs.waiting_on: you/OzGav: plugin vs #7173 design, landing page ownership; dmoo500: preview bounds
prs.tldr:
The rework does what OzGav asked. Resolve, preview and import all go through core matching, and the direct Deezer/iTunes/YTM calls are gone.
Our problems (3) and (4) are fixed. Problem (2) is only partly fixed: preview is paged and capped at 2 concurrent tracks, but limit has no upper bound and guests can call it.
Problem (1) still stands. share.music-assistant.io does not resolve and the landing page still lives in dmoo500/music-assistant-share.
Maintainers still have to choose between this plugin and jetersen's core share API (#7173 + models#447).
Tests: 151 pass, on the PR head and when merged with origin/dev. Core is barely touched: one private helper in helpers/compare.py is renamed to public.
prs.summary: Since 8d940da2a the plugin was split into payload.py, links.py and resolver.py. Track resolution now does an external-ID lookup via controller.get_item_by_external_id, gated by compare_track_evidence >= LIKELY plus ISRC corroboration, and falls back to tracks.enrich_provider_mappings. Album and artist resolution use core search with compare_album/compare_artist, and ambiguous results stay unresolved. Import sends M3U with SAME_RECORDING, which maps to the same LIKELY threshold, so preview and import agree. Status of our earlier problems: (1) NOT fixed. The default domain has no DNS record and the landing page is still in a personal repo. (2) PARTIAL. There is offset/limit paging (default 50), a semaphore of 2 and dedupe of identical tracks, but no maximum limit and no cap on payload size when decoding. Each track can still trigger up to 3 external-ID lookups times P providers plus P searches. That fan-out now goes through MA's own providers, which is the accepted pattern. (3) FIXED. Deezer and iTunes calls are removed, so only the user's own configured providers are queried. (4) FIXED. Core evidence matching is used, ISRC hits need the title and credited artists to agree, and version mismatches are rejected. The remaining gap is the explicit flag, which dmoo500 declined to carry. OzGav's points: own matcher, fixed (core). Hard-coded service URLs, mostly fixed: links now come only from ProviderMapping.url, but host tables are kept to compact and validate refs, and an artwork CDN allowlist remains (his call). Direct Deezer/iTunes, fixed. M3U with share:// paths, kept as agreed, with a plugin-side delimiter guard that works around generate_m3u not escaping '||'. Security: all four commands are authenticated (generate/resolve/preview need LIBRARY_READ, which guests have; import needs LIBRARY_WRITE). The old public HTTP/CORS resolve route is gone. There is no server-side state and no token, and the payload sits in the URL fragment, so there is nothing to guess or enumerate. Resolution respects per-user music-source visibility, through core filtering plus an explicit visible provider set. There is no rate limiting, so a guest can call preview with a huge limit. Outside the plugin: helpers/compare.py (rename _track_artist_credits_match to compare_track_artist_credits, no other callers on dev), translations/en.json (generated from strings.json) and a new test in tests/providers/builtin/test_import_matching.py. All 39 review threads are resolved. The PR merges cleanly onto origin/dev, which is 67 commits ahead of the merge base. The checklist ticks a docs PR, but none exists.

prs.title: Fix Roku Media Assistant player queue stalls and end-of-stream detection
prs.author: kees
prs.merge_state: merge-tree clean on origin/dev 4360495c4; review required, no auto-merge
prs.tldr: Approve: provider-only Roku fix (104 changed non-test lines). Advance and end-of-stream logic is sound and matches the app source. 34 tests pass. Nits only: lock hold during retries, INFO noise, long comments. Replaces draft #6458. Copilot was requested at 08:01Z; with "Approval recommended" it qualifies for auto-approval next run.
prs.summary: Provider-only change (roku_media_assistant/player.py +93/-11; 72 added code lines plus 21 added comment lines; tests +272). Verified against the Roku app source (MedievalApple/Media-Assistant mediaplayer.brs): handleDeepLink sets m.queuedDeeplink = Invalid on every play, including the blank ' ' stop deeplink, so clearing self.queued in play_media/stop matches the app. The 't':'m' flow metadata push does not touch the slot. Track-advance detection: dev swapped current_media to queued on any |jump| > 10 s, even with queued None, which blanked current_media and caused false advances on fresh plays, seeks and slow polls. Now it needs queued set and the position falling back by more than 10 s, and play_media resets the baseline to 0. No double advance: queued is consumed once and the app overwrites its single slot. Remote-control rewind of more than 10 s with an item queued still reads as an advance, but that already happens on dev. End-of-stream: IDLE only when state is 'play', position >= duration - 1.5 and the position has not moved for at least 10 s (three polls at 5 s). A normal track end with an item queued resets the position, so it does not trip. Pause maps to PAUSED and is excluded, mid-track buffering or stalls are not near the end, and radio/flow usually report no duration. The resulting IDLE feeds _handle_end_of_queue, which now finishes the queue on the last track (on dev it stayed PLAYING forever), and is ignored mid-queue because next_item is set. The 'stream ended' log fires once per stream. No timers or tasks are added: only two state fields and an asyncio.sleep inside the enqueue call, which is cancellable, so nothing needs cleanup on stop/unload. Flow mode never enqueues, so advance detection is inert there. The enqueue retry runs under the strict PLAYBACK lock, which is the only trade-off worth a note.

prs.title: Raumfeld: default ICY metadata to basic
prs.author: Simanias
prs.tldr: Ready: the one-time full-to-basic move now lives in config/migrations.py with a top-level marker, mirroring the Apple Music schedule migration, which is your placement rule. The old "deliberate full is overwritten" worry is gone: MA never stores a value equal to the default, so every stored "full" was written by the provider. Touches core (migrations.py, constants.py), so no auto-approve. 344 tests pass, Copilot approves, 2 nits.
prs.summary: The delta drops the per-player marker from the provider and adds _migrate_raumfeld_icy_basic in controllers/config/migrations.py, plus CONF_RAUMFELD_ICY_BASIC_MIGRATED in constants.py. It is modelled on _migrate_apple_music_sync_schedule. It returns early when the marker is set, returns False with no marker written when no player config has provider == "raumfeld" (the instance id is the domain, since multi_instance is false), rewrites values.enable_icy_metadata from "full" to "basic" in the raw dict, and then claims the marker even when nothing moved. migrate() runs in ConfigController._load before providers start and async_save()s when it returns True, so the heal runs once, before the provider's room sync. Scenarios: (1) no Raumfeld provider means no marker, which follows the 'marker only when relevant' rule; (2) a disabled provider or player keeps its player config in data and is healed too, which is correct because any stored "full" was written by the provider; (3) Raumfeld players added after the marker get "basic" from _ensure_icy_default and are never touched. Writing the raw dict instead of an API call matches every other migration; no API exists at that point, and the in-memory player config copy doesn't exist yet. Deliberate-"full" concern: it still holds and can't be fixed. PlayerConfig.to_raw() (music_assistant_models) keeps only values that differ from the entry default, and save_player_config stores new_raw wholesale. So under the old "full" default, a user who saved "full" never had it stored; every stored "full" came from _ensure_icy_default. After the migration "full" is non-default, so a later pick is stored and the marker keeps it. The provider side now writes "basic" only when nothing is stored. The entry switches from CONF_ENTRY_ICY_METADATA_DEFAULT_FULL (still used by bluesound) to a basic-default copy. Background: the provider only shipped in 2.11 betas (b3 onward), so only beta/nightly users have the stored "full". Pre-existing on dev and not caused by this PR: saving any Raumfeld player setting strips the default-valued ICY key from raw. The streams controller then reads the base default "disabled" until the next supervisor resync re-stores it. This is a possible follow-up, not a blocker. No API_SCHEMA_VERSION, MIN_SCHEMA_VERSION or DB schema change. The branch is one commit behind origin/dev (raumfeld/player.py only) and merges cleanly.

prs.title: Update Yandex Music Connect (Ynison) provider to v4.4.11: Ynison
prs.author: trudenboy
prs.waiting_on: you: post the replay finding (new patch) or `fix 7220`; trudenboy: 4 Copilot threads
prs.tldr: v4.4.11 fixes all three Copilot CRITICALs from the last round, and no Copilot thread is open. Our replay finding is half fixed: v4.4.10 handles our own Next racing the natural end, but a reconnect during the RADIO refill or a peer append during reconnect still streams the finished track again from 0. The new peer-status revision adds one more way to reach that replay.
prs.summary: Delta 17f7a4762..1f5b22413 (v4.4.11), provider and tests only. The dev merge in between adds nothing to the provider. (1) seed_start now seeds only when restart_reason is None, so a pending restart at 0 ms keeps its position and reason (Copilot r4402866110). (2) NavigationBaseline gets peer_status_revision. _parse_state bumps it when a non-relay status comes from another device under a new status version while the frame leaves player_queue unchanged. _matches_baseline compares it, so a peer seek or pause that lands while completion waits for the lock or reconnect supersedes the completion (r4402866339). Own progress reports, relays, own edit echoes that republish a retained peer status (same version) and peer option edits (queue changed) do not bump it. The tests cover each of these. (3) _confirmed_queue_version now advances only after the obsolete-own-echo check, so a rejected echo of navigation N cannot confirm it before N+1 is adopted (r4402866387). All three are correct as far as I can trace. (4) Standing finding, rerun at 1f5b22413. v4.4.10 already sends a superseded completion with a pending own navigation to that navigation's echo (pending_navigation_baseline), so probe_own_next_stream.py and probe_own_next_race.py now pass. probe_superseded_replay.py still fails on both cases (peer append during reconnect, reconnect during RADIO refill), streaming [t1, t1]. The SUPERSEDED branch is still `pass`. (5) The new revision makes one more path reach that branch. A peer status that bumps the revision but that _activate_playback does not treat as a seek requests no restart, and the loop replays the finished track from 0. Two examples are a status that arrives inside the post-reconnect settle window, which _handle_ynison_state skips, and a drift under 3 s. A real peer seek on the finished track does request a restart (drift is large because our position is at the track end), so that case follows the seek correctly. The new test parses the frame on the client alone, so it proves only the superseded outcome, not what plays next. (6) I rewrote the suggested patch. The own-navigation branch of the old patch is now redundant. The new patch retries completion once only when the finished item is still current, playback is unpaused on the same device, no restart or stop is pending, and navigation_version and peer_status_revision are unchanged, so it never overrides a peer seek or our own Next. With it, the suite (542) and all 5 probes pass. Without it, 2 probes fail. One known limit: if a peer replaces the queue with one whose current item is the same track at the same index and requests no restart, the retry advances past it. That is rarer than the replay it fixes. (7) The branch is 5 commits behind origin/dev 7a59e9b96, none of which touch the provider. No core files are touched.
