prs.title: Fix Bluesound metadata for library playback without an input ID
prs.author: imoamo72
prs.waiting_on: you: approve the Test workflow run (first-time contributor), then the merge queue
prs.ci: Test workflow action_required (first-time contributor); other checks green
prs.tldr: Auto-approved: the source-id fallback plus imoamo72's new trusts_reported_source opt-in, so a BluOS-app library session takes over MA's queue and its metadata shows. Opus checked MA playback keeps its queue (flow mode, announcements, synced followers, AirPlay output); 25 tests pass. One suggestion: for one poll after switching from the library back to MA, the old native source still shows (2-line patch). The Test workflow waits for your approval because imoamo72 is a first-time contributor.
prs.summary:
Delta since the last review: BluesoundPlayer sets _attr_trusts_reported_source = True, plus a test of the published source and metadata after an MA-to-library switch.

What trust changes: _resolve_source appends whatever it reports to source_list, so with trust on, any non-None _attr_active_source counts as a takeover in __reports_source_takeover. Checked each path on the PR head:
- MA's own stream (queue, flow mode, announcements, plugin /source/ URLs): every URL comes from streams.base_url, and _resolve_source sets None when the stream URL contains it. None is never a takeover, so the queue stays active.
- Grouped/synced BluOS: a follower sets the leader id as its source. That id is not in its source list, and __final_synced_to returns the leader's state before the takeover check anyway. A leader on its own library now shows LocalMusic to the whole group, which is correct.
- MA via a linked output protocol (AirPlay): a reported native source is overruled because active_output_protocol is not native. Behaviour unchanged.
- Presets and inputs: a preset reports its service (TuneIn and Tidal were already in EXTERNAL_SOURCES). A LocalMusic preset, Analog/Digital Input, HDMI ARC or an unknown input_id now take over the remembered MA queue as intended. Previously the MA queue kept showing over a TV or analog input.
- Idle player whose status still names a service: the reported-source branch requires playback_state != IDLE, so the source falls back to the MA source. Paused library playback shows LocalMusic and expires through the existing external-pause timeout (raw source, not affected by trust).
- Side effects are intended. With library or input playback active, MA's play/pause goes to the device source instead of resuming the MA queue. Announcements see the external prev_source. Protocol grouping is blocked while an external source plays.

The only path where MA's queue loses the source during MA playback is the optimistic play_media window (finding 1). The bluos_external fallback would also count as a takeover if BluOS ever reported a status with no stream URL, service or input during MA playback. I could not show that happens, so it is not flagged.

Hardware note: the PR body says it was verified on 2.10.8. Stable has no trust mechanism, so the takeover part has not been tested on a device. Worth asking the author to confirm on a dev build.

prs.title: Raumfeld: start a flow at least 8 s before the end of its first track
prs.author: Simanias
prs.tldr: Almost: the near-end restart works today, but its guard against an overriding Next/Previous reads core's private mass._tracked_timers and the "queue_play_index_<queue>" id string, so a core rename silently brings back the Copilot CRITICAL it fixes. Simpler: play_media already runs in the task holding the queue's re-entrant lock, so it can await play_index inline and drop the task, guard, cancel hook and faked PLAYING (patch attached, the 13 restart tests need rewriting). 279 tests pass, provider-only.
prs.summary: Re-review of the 4 commits since 7aac457c0. e6e26c342 reads the speed from the item's extra_attributes. 73a86b538 skips a correction that rounds to 0, which would otherwise trigger the resume-position restore. ca3539098 runs the restart as its own task under get_group_and_player_lock(queue_id, strict=True) and skips it when a queue_play_index timer or a live task exists. 8224a23ac ignores a done task and the originating task. Checked against origin/dev core. next/previous are handle_play_action (they take the same lock), move current_index right away and call_later(1, play_index, task_id=queue_play_index_<q>). play_index cancels that timer at entry. call_later pops the timer before creating the task under the same id. get_player_lock is re-entrant per task. So: a Next ahead of the restart leaves a timer and the restart skips. A Next whose timer already fired leaves a live task waiting on the lock and the restart skips. A Next behind the restart runs after it. A stop, seek, play or pause hits _changes_playback and cancels the restart. I found no path that leaves the room silent for good. The failure cases are a ResourceBusyError after the 120 s strict wait (unhandled, unlike _play_next) and a cancel while the restart is already inside play_index (pause does not take the queue lock, so it aborts the play halfway). Both are narrow, and a poll corrects the faked PLAYING state. The design cost is the coupling: no other provider touches mass._tracked_timers (only profiler and diagnostics), and the guard encodes how core's next/previous schedule work. The inline alternative works because play_index, players.play_media, _handle_play_media, the sync group and the provider's play_media are all awaited in one task. The re-entrant lock lets a nested play_index run, Next/Previous/seek wait behind it like behind any play, and the provider's own optimistic PLAYING at the end of the inner play_media satisfies both wait_for_player_update calls. The precondition is that play_media is reached from the task holding the queue lock. Every core path meets it, and _play_next holds the same lock for its own queue. Copilot's latest review (8224a23ac) has no open issues, and there are no unresolved threads. Cross-PR: conflicts with #7216 in 4 player.py hunks (adjacent inserts) and the test file. After resolving, the early return in play_media sits before #7216's announcement-state reset, which is harmless.

prs.title: Update ABC Radio Network Provider to support multiple states in Australia
prs.author: genesispc
prs.tldr: Almost: a state picker (default NSW) selects the local ABC feeds for Triple J, Double J, Classic and ABC Kids and the matching now-playing timezone, and now-playing moves to ABC's core-next API. Existing installs keep NSW streams and the same item ids, so favourites stay intact; Opus checked every regional URL and the new endpoint live. Only gap: no tests at all, while the checklist ticks "tests added". Opus wrote 9 tests that pass on the head.
prs.summary: Adds a CONF_STATE ConfigEntry (ConfigEntryType.STRING, single value, 7 options nsw/vic/qld/sa/nt/wa/tas, default nsw) returned from the instance-level get_config_entries, which is the current provider API. Changing it reloads the provider through the default update_config. Station ids, item ids and provider mappings are unchanged (parse_radio untouched), so library items, favourites and playlists stay stable. With no stored value, the default nsw resolves to exactly the old stream URLs. The one URL change is kidslisten, abckids.m3u8 -> abckidsnsw.m3u8, and both playlists point to the same akamai abckidsnsw rendition. Per-station regions match the CDN: triplej/doublej/abckids have nsw/qld/sa/nt/wa (vic/tas 404), classic also has vic. States without a local feed fall back to the NSW stream and the Sydney tz, which is the right wall clock for VIC/TAS/ACT. National stations always use their single URL and the Sydney tz. The now-playing API moved from music.abcradio.net.au/api/v1/plays/{id}/now.json to www.abc.net.au/core-next/api/musicNowPlaying/{ID}?tz=..., using upper-cased station ids. All 9 codes return 200, tz really shifts the result (Sydney/Adelaide/Perth gave different tracks), and an unknown code gives 500, which the existing status check turns into None. mapiNow null (talk) -> None, and _update_stream_metadata clears stale info as before. Security review: MA's own scope check still gates every call, unknown scopes fail closed, and the smart_playlists bypass is fixed. One gap (GPT Sol, confirmed by Opus): party/ and music_quiz/ listen_in accept a web_player_id outside a user's player filter, which MCP blocks for set_members. prs.summary:
Since 2c593439b (v2.2.3) the PR adds: (1) a scope fallback in command_policy for commands outside every family (provider-registered), using SCOPE_FAMILIES; (2) the smart_playlists/ family mapped to playlist capabilities; (3) exact overrides where the declared scope understates the effect: party/skip needs control:playback, party/add_to_queue and boost_queue_item need edit:queue plus control:playback, party/url needs system:admin (it mints a guest user and join code), and yandex_station/command needs system:admin; (4) a guest refusal in the Connect wizard token mint (MA only enforces this in auth/token/create, I confirmed it on dev at controllers/webserver/auth.py:1349); (5) an RFC 9728 resource_metadata route so the 401 WWW-Authenticate names the metadata URL.
I resolved every in-tree provider command on dev through the PR's resolve_command_policy. ai_radio writes and deletes map to config:write:provider and the reads to config:read or query:library; queue_dj maps to edit:queue. ambient_sounds add maps to edit:library and remove to delete:library. builtin add_track/add_radio map to edit:library. hass/search_control_entities maps to config:read. music_quiz host commands (users.invite) and guest commands (scope None) are hard-denied. Listen-in and sendspin/pair_web_player map to control:players (pairing still needs the web player's own pairing token). profiler/report maps to system:admin. sonic_similarity rebuild maps to edit:library, the rest to query:library. Nothing admin-only, destructive or config-changing lands on a lower MCP capability than its MA scope implies.
Tuple scopes use the weakest member, which matches MA's any-of grant. A destructive verb under a read-only scope is hard-denied.
With require_auth disabled (an explicit admin opt-out, default on) the MA scope check is skipped and provider commands run with no current_user, but the same already held for core commands on dev.

prs.title: Fix AI Radio opening intro and first transition scheduling
prs.author: adamlonsdale
prs.waiting_on: you: core hook call (AI Radio intro); adamlonsdale: OzGav's threads
prs.ci: pytest (2/3) failed on a uv install network error (infra, rerun)
prs.tldr: Not ready: the bug is real (the show DJ plans after play_index already handed items 0 and 1 to the player), but the PR reintroduces the opening intro you left out of #6372 via a new core on_queue_start plugin hook, and its AI Radio side duplicates _replan_queue, reworks DJ locking and adds multi-clip slots that change normal replans. Show start also waits on the weather lookup (up to 20 s). A provider-only fix is possible via the queue-items event that already runs before play_index. OzGav requested changes too.
prs.summary:
Adds PluginProvider.on_queue_start, awaited by QueueLoaderMixin._start_queue before play_index for PLAY/REPLACE, with a broad except that logs and still starts playback (CancelledError propagates). AI Radio implements it: under _dj_lock it arms a fresh show state, awaits weather tokens, re-reads the queue, plans every slot including start_of_playlist over the upcoming show, splices clips with guard -2 (so the intro can sit at the start index), publishes in one update_items, sets boundary mix and persists. It also reworks set_queue_dj into _set_queue_dj with automatic arming under the lock, moves _maybe_detach_show_dj under the lock, groups multiple sections that share a slot (_splice_dj_slot) for both on_queue_start and _replan_queue, and teaches _repair_dj_clips about grouped slots.

Root cause on dev: _ensure_show_dj runs eagerly inside load()'s QUEUE_ITEMS_UPDATED dispatch and arms the state in memory before play_index. It then suspends at _write_queue_dj, and the replan task awaits _prepare_runtime_tokens on top of that. By the time it plans, committed_index covers items 0 and 1, so the first gap is too_close. _replan_queue only ever allows between_songs and end_of_playlist, so an intro is never planned. The PR body calls this a b7 regression, but #6372 (3b90f39dea) states 'The intro is not played: putting it in front of the first track would need the core to accept sound effects from a provider feed.' The intro half is new behaviour on top of that decision.

Core hook vs provider-only: a core-free fix is possible. get_radio_tracks is awaited by the core before load(), so AI Radio can warm the weather cache there. The QUEUE_ITEMS_UPDATED handler runs eagerly (mass.create_task eager_start=True) inside load(), before play_index, so a synchronous arm plus opening plan plus update_items there would land before playback. dev already relies on that ordering for set_boundary_mix_required ('decided at the play start this arm precedes'). The catch is that it depends on implicit eager-dispatch ordering and a reentrant update_items inside load(). The explicit hook is about 25 lines of core and easier to reason about. If you want intros, the hook is defensible. The AI Radio side should then be small: on_queue_start arms the state and runs one _replan_queue pass with an opening flag (allow start_of_playlist, pre-play guard), not a second copy of the planner.

Error handling: OzGav's and Bot-MArley's ask is addressed. _start_queue catches Exception per plugin, logs plugin name and queue id, keeps the last good start_index and still calls play_index. CancelledError propagates. Still open: AI Radio raises InvalidDataError for an expected race (queue changed during weather), which the core logs as an exception with traceback. There is also no time bound on the hook.

Non-AI-Radio queues: every PLAY/REPLACE now awaits each plugin's on_queue_start sequentially. The base returns immediately, and AI Radio returns early when no show station is in the queue sources, so the cost is negligible today. Resume, seek, next and play_index from the queue UI never call the hook. Neither does the dynamic-mode start at queue_loader.py:1166, which is irrelevant for a finite show.

Tests: thorough but heavy, about 490 new lines in test_queue_dj.py, most of them chasing races Copilot raised over five iterations. The core tests are fine. The three-plugin start_index chaining test covers a scenario with one real implementer. There is a real-path test for eager event dispatch during loading. No test changes affect existing behaviour.

Open threads: OzGav 'catch expected errors' (queue_loader.py:251) and Bot-MArley's matching thread are addressed in code but unresolved. OzGav's docstring thread (plugin.py:81) is not addressed. OzGav's scope question in the conversation (why the locking rework, multi-clip slots and duplicated planning) has no reply.

prs.title: Hold both queues' playback locks while a queue is transferred
prs.author: mnestrud
prs.waiting_on: you: the turn-lock trade-off; then a lab rerun
prs.gpt_sol: 1 problem (deadlock against cmd_set_members powering on a member with auto-play)
prs.tldr: The lock race is real and the PR closes it for plain transfers, and all tests pass. But Copilot's open CRITICAL r4395432985 is real: I reproduced a transfer and a leadership handover each holding a lock the other waits for, until the 120 s strict timeout fails the transfer. The global turn plus the in-turn bypass is the fourth deadlock design in three commits; a two-phase transfer (source chain, then target chain, never both) would drop most of the 163 lines.
prs.summary: transfer_queue now runs under get_playback_locks(source, target, strict=True). That covers the #6779 race where play_index/resume/stop on either queue interleaved with a transfer. _transfer_ad_hoc_leadership holds both leaders through transfer, regroup and resume. The new primitive adds a process-wide turn lock, a bypass for tasks that already hold a playback lock, a retry loop when ownership changed during the wait, and an early-release callable. Earlier CRITICALs r4389512413, r4389512498, r4392794816 and r4392794907 are fixed on 6442a5071. The bypass reopens the inversion the turn exists to prevent: a transfer that planned [a, c] while a was standalone holds a and waits for c, while a cmd_ungroup(c) that got c first hands leadership to a (now a member after a concurrent join), skips the turn and waits for a. With scaled timeouts the repro ends with both waiting the full strict timeout and the transfer raising ResourceBusyError. In production that is 120 s, with every other transfer queued behind the turn. The turn also leaves out other nested two-chain acquirers such as stream_feeder._stop_paused_slot_holder, which runs inside a play action. Each review round has found a new interleaving, so the design itself is fragile rather than any one line. Holding one chain at a time (source phase, then target phase, each through the existing handle_play_action) gives the same protection against play actions without hold-and-wait across chains, so no turn, bypass, replan loop or release callable is needed.

prs.title: Name the session a stream or queue is loaded into
prs.author: mnestrud
prs.tldr: Adds an optional sync on_session(session_id) callback to play_stream_url and play_cloud_queue, fired right after the session exists and before the load is sent. It does not change any exception: it is additive and keyword-defaulted, so every current caller and except clause behaves as before. The logic is correct and all 147 tests pass. Nothing in the server uses it yet: it needs an aiosonos release, a pin bump from 0.1.15 and a Sonos provider change, and no server PR (including #7235) contains that.
prs.summary: Design: the PR uses a callback rather than a new exception type or attribute. That is the less invasive choice. CommandTimeout, FailedCommand, InvalidState and CancelledError all propagate unchanged, so existing except clauses still catch everything. A callback also covers CancelledError, which an exception attribute could not. The callback is called synchronously inside _session_lock, after _create_playback_session returns (or the active session is reused) and before the load await. So: callback fired means the load may have gone out, and callback not fired means nothing was loaded. That holds for creation timeouts, evictions during subscribe (FailedCommand) and cleanup (InvalidState), because all of them raise before the call. If the callback has fired and the load is then refused, the caller still has to tell the cases apart by exception type, as it does today. The internal _play_stream_url('clear', None) caller in stop/clear is unaffected because the default is None. Server callers (origin/dev, aiosonos==0.1.15): player.py play_media calls play_cloud_queue twice (announcement and queue) and _play_stream calls play_stream_url once, all positionally without on_session, so all stay compatible. To get the benefit, _play_stream needs to capture the session via on_session and pass it to _settle_failed_load in place of the replaced_session_id comparison. The queue path can use it too, in place of reading group.active_session_id after the failure. No server PR does this: #7235 is the transfer_queue lock work and has no aiosonos or on_session changes. Tests: 4 focused tests for ordering (await_count is 0 when the callback fires), no call on a failed creation, a call on an unanswered load, and reuse of the active session for queues. They are clear and minimal. The only gaps are listed below.

prs.title: Fix Spotify on Soloist stopping the queue at the end of every track
prs.author: MarvinSchenkel
prs.waiting_on: OzGav (or another maintainer): approve; reporter confirmed
prs.tldr: The fix is correct and small. A pause now arms a 2 s run-scoped watch, and the queue only stops if the engine is still paused and the run is still live at the deadline. The engine's end-of-item pause is followed within milliseconds by exit, wander or delivery done, so it no longer stops the queue. #7117's intent holds: an app pause still stops the queue, about 2 s later. 296 tests pass, and the PR applies cleanly to stable with its tests green there, so backport it.
prs.summary: Logic checked against origin/dev (soloist.py has no changes on dev since the merge base). Source of truth: the watch re-checks run state (_engine_exited via proc.wait, _item_over via wander, _delivery_done, _stopped, _error) at the deadline. It never looks at the next track, so a next track that starts late does not matter. Real app pause near track end: the engine stops, never exits, and the queue stops after 2 s with the resume position kept. Pause then resume (playing or buffering) within the grace: no stop. Repeated pause: the old watch is cancelled and a new deadline set. Seek, including to near the end: the old run is stopped (watch cancelled through _tasks), and the new run's cold seek runs with _reader None, so nothing arms during startup. Last track of the queue: the engine exits after its pause, nothing stops, and the queue ends naturally (2.10.8 stopped it, which was harmless). Flow mode: same per-item run, no difference. Teardown: the watch goes through _spawn_task, so stop(), unload(), discard_run and a new play all cancel it, and _item_live() checks _stopped, so a watch cannot be armed after stop(). The stop is fired through mass.create_task rather than awaited, so stop() cannot cancel-join its own caller. Autoplay on: the wander sets _item_over before or right after the pause, and arming now also covers buffering->paused, which is still dismissed by the wander. Trade-offs that remain: after a pause in the Spotify app, MA keeps playing up to 2 s of cushioned audio before the stop (well under the 20 s stall watchdog). Also, if an account takeover reports paused before the device goes inactive, the _fail path now wins over the queue stop. That matches 2.10.7 behaviour and has not been verified. Regression test test_the_engine_pausing_at_its_items_end_does_not_stop_the_queue would fail on origin/dev. Tests use a 0.02 s grace against a 0.1 s sleep, which is deterministic because asyncio fires timers in deadline order.

prs.title: Keep other music sources' images when a library item is overwritten
prs.author: GoatsAndMonkeys
prs.tldr: Correct and narrow. On an overwrite, album and artist refreshes keep the stored images of linked sources other than the updating instance, the same way provider_mappings_for_update keeps their mappings. OpenSubsonic attributes images by instance id, so two Navidrome accounts on one domain are kept apart, which is the reported case. Two small points: the domain union in update_sources is unused except in one legacy edge case, and tracks still wipe on overwrite. Core code, so Marvin's call. No backport.
prs.summary: Image attribution: MediaItemImage.provider is the instance id for music providers in practice (opensubsonic parsers use instance_id everywhere; repo-wide ~170 instance-id uses against ~17 self.domain uses, all in metadata providers such as fanarttv/coverartarchive/itunes_artwork or in radio providers). kept_sources holds instance ids, so A's images (provider=subsonic_a) survive a refresh from subsonic_b, and domain-attributed metadata-provider images are dropped on overwrite as before (refresh_item re-runs update_metadata(force_refresh=True) right after, so they come back). Duplicates: add_image appends to a UniqueList keyed on (type, provider, path), so an exact repeat is skipped. The same Navidrome cover id under two instances is kept twice, which is needed because each one resolves only through its own instance. Ordering: the updating source's images come first and the kept ones are appended, so the raw first thumb is the last-refreshed source's. That matches the old behaviour, and preferred_thumb (#6708) already picks the right one per user. Other callers: only albums and artists pass mappings. Emby's overwrite with the library item itself puts every instance into update_sources, so nothing is kept and the result equals before. Tracks, playlists, audiobooks, podcasts, radio and genres keep `update.metadata if overwrite`, so a shared track still loses the other account's cover on a refresh (follow-up). Non-overwrite merges were never affected: MediaItemMetadata.update merges image lists, so a sync from both accounts already stores both. Tests: one helper test for keep, one for drop of unlinked and metadata-provider images, and one controller integration test on a test DB for artist and album. They cover the fix without redundancy. The PR is up to date with origin/dev and the helpers' callers are unchanged elsewhere. Stable: metadata_for_update has the same wipe, but stable has neither per-user music sources (helpers/provider_access.py is absent) nor #6708, so every instance's image loads for every user and the wipe has no visible effect there. The dry-run merge onto stable conflicts in tests/controllers/music/test_music_helpers.py.

prs.title: Stop the MusicBrainz link run reporting merged items as failed
prs.author: OzGav
prs.tldr: The guard reuses the existing _in_library check before the inter-item pause, so an item that has left the library is skipped with no failure, no warning and no budget spent. It is correct and cheap: one PK read per item, at most 50 per run. On dev the run cannot merge away a later item of its own batch. That only becomes reachable with #7212 (still open), or when a sync or user removes an item during a run. So the PR is safe to land in either order. 34 tests pass.
prs.summary: Verified against origin/dev (291ddf9198). _in_library (enrichment.py:788) does get_library_item and maps MediaNotFoundError to False, the same check update_metadata already uses at controller.py:364. Before this PR the stale item went to link_item_to_musicbrainz: it spent a MusicBrainz lookup, then update_item_in_library raised MediaNotFoundError (in _SCAN_ITEM_ERRORS), giving failed+1, a task failure and a warning. Placing the check before the sleep and progress update means a skipped item uses no budget and no wait, and 'processed' only counts items actually linked. Reachability: on dev the only in-run merge is merge_library_artists_by_mbid. It merges artists that already carry the mbid, and the artist phase only selects artists without an MB id. link_musicbrainz_mappings does not merge on mapping conflicts. So on dev the run cannot remove a later batch item itself; only a concurrent sync or delete can. With #7212 an identified artist in a relink phase can follow a MusicBrainz merge to an id that other artists in the same batch hold, and merge_library_artists_by_mbid keeps the lowest item_id. Because the batch is ordered by timestamp_added, a later batch item can then be the source. The test mocks get_library_item with [MediaNotFoundError, kept] and checks the item is skipped, the remaining one is linked, nothing is reported and the summary counts are right. It fails without the change, because the 'gone' album would be linked.

prs.title: Offer overlay volumes of a container as media locations
prs.author: GoatsAndMonkeys
prs.tldr: Lets a host overlay folder mapped into the container (the /media_unified case) show up in the folder picker. Container roots are matched by their storage layout, not by folder name. The container's own root and system paths stay out, and overlays are still never offered outside a container. Tests cover both the true and false cases. Only a pre-existing fuse-overlayfs gap and a comment nit remain.
prs.summary: Parsing is unchanged: the mountpoint is octal-unescaped, fstype comes after the separator, ro comes from the mount or super options. The new branch only admits fstype == overlay when in_container, the mountpoint is not '/', is not within SYSTEM_PATHS / CONTAINER_RESERVED_PATHS / the server folders, and does not end in a container-storage root. I checked the root patterns: Docker overlay2 (any data-root, snap Docker, Unraid), legacy overlay, Podman/CRI-O rootful and rootless, containerd/k3s task rootfs, and Docker with the containerd image store all match. I ran probes: /media/merged, /rootfs and /pool/overlay/merged are offered, and Podman image mounts and ':O' overlay volumes are offered as real volumes. HA OS add-on: the fixture holds only the '/' overlay, so nothing changes there. Plain Docker: only '/' is overlay unless the user maps an overlay folder or the whole container storage. k8s/containerd and LXC have no /.dockerenv or /run/.containerenv, so in_container is False there and overlays stay excluded. That is a false negative only, and it predates this PR. Exposure: in a container, _is_visible shows every MEDIA location to non-admin users too, so a missed container root would leak. All overlay container-root layouts I could name are caught. A '/:/host' mapping still exposes non-container overlays such as /host/usr (systemd-sysext), but the same mapping already exposes ext4 mounts on dev, so this is the user's choice. Nothing on origin/dev touched storage since the merge base, and the PR merges cleanly. Core code, so Marvin approves.

prs.title: Show each item once in recently played
prs.author: GoatsAndMonkeys
prs.waiting_on: GoatsAndMonkeys: shrink to the dedupe only (your 13:58Z ask)
prs.tldr:
recently_played LEFT JOINs provider_mappings on its unique key, so provider rows resolve to their library item. It streams rows newest first and keeps the first row per item until limit distinct items are found.
With a user filter the (userid,timestamp) index serves the ORDER BY and the read stops early. Without one it sorts the whole joined playlog (fine at realistic sizes).
mark_item_unplayed now clears every alias and signals only the aliases it actually deleted. All Copilot threads are resolved, CI green, 1615 tests pass.
Only SUGGESTION/NIT level notes.
prs.summary: Dedupe key is (media_type, entry_provider, entry_item_id), where provider rows that map to a library item become ('library', CAST(l.item_id AS TEXT)). That matches how library rows store p.item_id. Ordering is timestamp DESC, rowid DESC, so the newest alias wins and ties are deterministic. Limit counts distinct entries, 0 still means all, and the API has no offset, so there is no paging issue. The media type, user_initiated, always_include, fully_played, userid, queue_id, played_after and provider/visible-source filters still apply per row before the dedupe. A merged entry is only listed if at least one of its rows passes the filter. I measured query plans on a synthetic 200k-row playlog. With a userid: SEARCH via userid_timestamp_idx, the join is a unique-index lookup, no temp sort, first 10 rows in 0.1 ms (same as before). Without a userid (background callers with no session user): SCAN plus temp B-tree over all joined rows, 182 ms against 24 ms before (where LIMIT allowed a top-N sort). The table is unique per item/provider/user, so real sizes are far smaller. On mark_item_unplayed: aliases are the given key, its library item, and all of the library item's mappings. Deletes run per user per alias, and events only go out for aliases whose delete hit a row (the given item always gets one). The 'private alias broadcast' Copilot raised is no different from mark_item_played, which already broadcasts PLAYLOG_UPDATED to all clients. The latest Copilot overview at head 5346fccda lists no open issues.

prs.title: Clear a provider's cache after it is reconfigured
prs.author: GoatsAndMonkeys
prs.waiting_on: GoatsAndMonkeys: 2 Copilot CRITICALs (category 1 kept, combined search kept)
prs.tldr: Down to about 30 lines of logic: reconfigure now unloads the instance, clears its cache through a public MusicController.clear_provider_cache, then reloads it. The private-key import and the non-atomic snapshot rewrite are gone. But exclude_category=1 keeps everything any provider stores in category 1, including Tidal's personalised pages and Overcast's OPML. The combined search cache also survives, and both are open Copilot CRITICALs on the head. A 10-line patch fixes both.
prs.summary: The delta drops the race guards (listing generations, cancelling flight tasks by name, unloading checks in use_cache and recommendation_payload) and accepts that a lost race serves old data until it expires. What is left: _finish_provider_reconfigure calls unload_provider, then clear_provider_cache, then load_provider_config, and any error restores the old setup_data. clear_provider_cache runs cache.clear(provider LIKE '%id%', persistent = 0, category != 1), deletes the persistent recommendations payload, and drops every library:// listing. Verified: 2302 tests pass across tests/controllers/cache, config, music and tests/models/test_recommendation_payload.py. The problem is that CACHE_CATEGORY_PREV_LIBRARY_IDS = 1 is not reserved. At least 17 providers use category 1 for their own data: Tidal recommendation pages (personalised, keyed by page path), Overcast OPML (the account's subscriptions), Audible and Storytel audiobooks, gpodder sync state, opensubsonic podcast channels, Pandora feedback and Apple Music decrypt keys. Excluding the whole category keeps all of that across an account switch. A scratch repro through the reconfigure flow confirms it: a category-1 'pages/home' entry survives. Combined search results are cached under provider 'music' and survive as well (confirmed). They are dropped at the next sync completion or after SEARCH_CACHE_EXPIRATION_COMBINED. Fix: keep only the snapshot keys (media type values) in category 1, and delete category 10 for 'music'. Both are in suggested_fix, and 2283 cache/config/music tests pass with it. The rest is unchanged from last time and low impact. The LIKE '%id%' match also hits airplay_receiver, hass_players, spotify_connect and sendspin_* when airplay, hass, spotify or sendspin is reconfigured, but the substring is what removes the 'id://...' listing keys, and the cost is one refetch. The clear also runs for every reconfigure (about 70 providers with run_setup, any reason). If cache.clear itself fails, the provider stays unloaded with the old credentials restored. The PR has a test for the credentials but none for a reload. Without the guards, an in-flight old-instance listing fill or use_cache call can still write after the clear. The window is a request's duration, and the author accepted it.

prs.title: Match an album's tracks to MusicBrainz in order when the whole album lines up
prs.author: OzGav
prs.tldr: Sound idea and conservative gates (exact count, 1..n per disc, every length within 8 s, local files excluded, existing recording id respected). The one gap: the order match ignores the ISRCs and recording ids the tracks already carry, so a swapped pair of similar-length tracks takes each other's recordings and ISRCs even when the service's own ISRCs say otherwise. A small guard fixes it. Tests pass (307). GPT Sol adds that disc numbers themselves are not checked (only disc 2, or discs 1 and 3, still pass).
prs.summary: _link_tracks_to_release now first asks _recordings_in_order for a per-track recording: per streaming domain, the tracks that are only on streaming providers are sorted by (disc or 1, number), must equal the release's flattened track count, be numbered 1..n on each disc, and every length must be within _TRACK_DURATION_TOLERANCE (8 s) of the release track (release-track length preferred over recording length). If so each track takes the recording at its flat index, unless it already holds a different recording id. Anything else falls back to the old position + title check. Risk review: different edition with a different count, bonus tracks, a hidden track folded into the last track, and continuous numbering across discs (disc 2 numbered 11..20) are all rejected and fall back. A service that puts every disc on disc 1 numbered 1..N is accepted and maps correctly. A remaster with the same count and lengths usually shares MB recordings, so the risk there is low. The remaining hole is reordering: a swap of two tracks within 8 s of each other (common on pop albums, and possible when resolve_release picks a sibling release with a different running order, e.g. vinyl vs CD) passes every gate. 8 s catches an off-by-one shift across the album but not a local swap. Existing data: fill_track_from_recording never overwrites an existing mbid, and the new `track.mbid in (None, recording.id)` guard also stops ISRCs from a different recording being added. So user-set and #7261 ISRC-derived recording ids are not overwritten. But that check is per track, so a track holding the recording id of another position (proof of misalignment) does not stop its neighbours from being assigned in order. ISRCs are not unique external ids, so a wrong order match permanently adds a foreign ISRC to the track, and _matching_provider_track then uses it to link provider tracks. Merges cleanly onto origin/dev (#7261 only touched the MusicBrainz provider).

prs.title: Fix a restarted Squeezelite group member staying silent
prs.author: MarvinSchenkel
prs.gpt_sol: 1 problem (by design: native-group member ends ungrouped)
prs.tldr:
Correct, minimal provider-side fix: the leader drops a member on a real slimproto disconnect and on the reconnect race aioslimproto never reports.
synced_to is still resolvable at both call sites (player not yet unregistered), so the lookup works.
Leader stream is untouched (dropped subscriber just leaves MultiClientStream); a re-add goes through set_members -> cmd_resume.
29/29 squeezelite tests pass, CI green, backport merges cleanly onto stable.
prs.summary: PLAYER_DISCONNECTED: aioslimproto fires it only when the reader loop ends (EOF/timeout/reset), so it is a real connection end. The provider releases the member from its leader before scheduling unregister, while the old MA player is still registered and base Player.synced_to (available players, same provider) still resolves the leader. PLAYER_CONNECTED: when aioslimproto sees a HELO for an id whose old client is no longer connected but was never popped (disconnect() via send_frame cancels the reader, so no DISCONNECTED is emitted), it replaces the client silently; the PR covers this by releasing the still-registered old player before the new SqueezelitePlayer is set up. A first connect is a no-op (get_player returns None), and a duplicate live connection is rejected inside aioslimproto before the event reaches MA. Leader stream: the member's HTTP subscriber drops with its socket, MultiClientStream keeps feeding the others, and remove_disconnected_member intentionally does not restart. The leader clears its list when only itself remains, matching set_members. Member that never returns: dropped on DISCONNECTED; in the silent send_frame path it stays listed until it reconnects (pre-existing aioslimproto behaviour, chip already planned). User ungroup/regroup meanwhile: set_members could never remove a disconnected member (it iterates live slim clients), so this PR fixes that too; a regroup after reconnect adds normally. Leader restart: synced_to is None so nothing happens; the new leader object starts with empty members, so the members come back ungrouped. Unchanged by this PR.

prs.title: Stop showing a disconnected player's queue as playing
prs.author: MarvinSchenkel
prs.tldr: The fix is right: on_player_remove publishes the dropped queue once as idle, and the protocol transition now drops the queue before PLAYER_REMOVED. The AI Radio guards are needed and correct. One regression: the flow-mode _resume_on_idle task now treats the removal's IDLE as the player finishing and raises KeyError on the gone queue (reproduced). The fix is a one-line identity check. Backport alongside #7249 without the AI Radio hunks.
prs.summary: on_player_remove pops the queue data, sets its PlayerQueue.state to IDLE and signals QUEUE_UPDATED. It runs for both a non-permanent unregister (then PLAYER_UPDATED available=False) and a permanent one (then PLAYER_REMOVED), and in both cases the queue update goes out before the player event. The pending cache save was already cancelled earlier in the method, and _save_queue_to_cache/signal_update guard on _queue_data, so the IDLE mutation is never persisted. On reconnect, on_player_register restores from cache into a new PlayerQueueData and re-derives the state through on_player_update. Resume and position behave as on dev. In _finish_player_type_transition the queue now goes before PLAYER_REMOVED, so the frontend cannot re-add the queue after dropping the player. Sync leaders and groups: only the dropped player's own queue changes. Members are inactive anyway, and signal_update for a missing queue is a no-op. Server-side QUEUE_UPDATED subscribers (sendspin, sonos hand-over check, plex_connect, snapcast socket server, websocket filter) all cope with a missing queue. The AI Radio change is needed: the new event reaches _on_dj_queue_event, where player_queues.get() returns None. Without the guards, _maybe_detach_show_dj would detach the show DJ and _forget_armed_show would drop the arm-once record, so a returning player could re-arm a DJ the user had turned off. PLAYER_REMOVED still drops both. Flaw: queue_buffer_completed starts _resume_on_idle, which holds the PlayerQueue object. Before this PR a removed queue stayed PLAYING and the loop timed out harmlessly. Now, if the player drops within 60 s of its flow stream finishing generation (e.g. a speaker switched off during the tail of the last track), the loop sees IDLE and calls get_next_item, and _get_next_index then raises KeyError on _queue_data[queue_id]. A simulation reproduces it: KeyError 'q1' on the PR, a clean finish on dev. If the player re-registers within that second, it can play_index on the restored queue instead. Tests: 1621 passed across player_queues, the player controller and ai_radio. The new tests cover the idle publish (both permanent values), the event order and the AI Radio survival, but not the flow resume path. CI is green and Copilot is clean.

prs.summary: The PR went from 227 lines and 9 state fields to 72 lines and 2 fields (_first_position, _position_moved). Until the reported position moves on the current track, it is adopted once. After that MA's own clock runs: a pause holds it, a resume continues it, IDLE resets it to 0. Once the position moves, the renderer is followed exactly as on dev. Verified: 51 DLNA tests pass, and 6 of the new tests fail on dev's player.py. I added scratch repros with the PR's own helpers. A normal renderer paused outside MA at 20 s, noticed at 40 s and then updated again while paused stays at 20 and reads 30 ten seconds after the resume (the old head showed 40, then 50). A backward seek to 5 while paused shows 5 and then 9. A 0.5 s pause on a 0/None renderer continues correctly. A stop starts over at 0 (PR test). The only window left for a normal renderer is before its second distinct report. It needs a pause in the same second as the first report and is not realistic. One rule changed since the last head: _playing_since is no longer reset on a URI change. In non-flow mode (gapless enqueue, not the DLNA default) a stuck-at-0 renderer that moves to the next URI by itself is read from the event. No GetPositionInfo poll runs then, so the 00:00:00 stamp is the last poll's, up to 30 s old. It is adopted with that anchor and never re-read, so the whole track runs ahead (repro: 35 s shown after 10 s). For a renderer reporting None the clock simply carries on from the previous track; Copilot's open CRITICAL at :182 is the same gap. seek() does not move MA's clock either, so a non-flow seek on a stuck renderer is lost. In flow mode a seek goes through play_media and resets everything. Both cases are no worse than dev, which re-anchors 0 at every poll, but the PR now owns the clock for these renderers. Copilot's other open CRITICAL (:669, a cached 200 at STOPPED followed by a fixed 0) cannot happen for MA-started playback, because play_media resets both fields, and a stuck renderer reports 0 while stopped too. Also: the reset now fires when the device reports an empty URI (the previous head required a non-empty one), and that restarts the stuck clock at 0. prs.copilot_note: Approval recommended on fec84206f.
prs.summary: MA seeks on WiiM always go through play_index/play_media with a stream that starts at the seek offset, so the device's position restarts at 0 for each handover. In the wiim 0.3.1 SDK, current_media.uri comes from the AVTransportURIMetaData event, which echoes MA's own DIDL right after SetAVTransportURI. current_media.position is _current_position, which only changes on a GetPositionInfo RelTime read (integer seconds, clamped at >= 0), a RelativeTimePosition/A_ARG_TYPE_SeekTarget event, or not at all when RelTime is missing. So the new URI shows up next to the old stream's position, exactly as the PR describes, and the existing _ma_stream_uri guard (end-of-stream check) let it through. The new guard is _ma_stream_sent = (url, monotonic), set just before async_play and dropped when async_play fails or on seek(). A position is ignored while it is larger than time since handover plus 2 s. A real reading can't trip it: the stream starts at 0, a pause only lowers the position against the clock, and RelTime truncates down. The guard ends at the first plausible reading that is not at the stream's end and is either nonzero or PLAYING at 0. That covers both Copilot CRITICALs (the 1 s stream at its end, and PLAYING at 0 followed by an app seek), and each has a test. The only path that can still be blocked is a WiiM Home app seek forward while the stream is still loading, before any accepted reading. That is a sub-second window and it self-heals as time passes. A stale reading of 2 s or less (a seek within ~2 s of the previous handover) still gets through and ends the guard, so the error there is at most 2 s. Followers read the leader's state and have no guard of their own. Gapless enqueue changes the URI away from the guarded one, so it is unaffected. elapsed is only written in _sync_position, so no other path bypasses the guard. stop() keeps _ma_stream_sent on purpose (test_stopped_stream_still_loading_keeps_its_start_position). Copilot threads are answered, with fixes in ab304ec4d and fec84206f.

prs.summary: set_members now creates the leader's resume under task_id squeezelite_regroup_resume_<leader> with abort_existing=True. In the announcement flow the announcement holds the leader's PLAYBACK lock (get_group_and_player_lock) across remove, clip and re-add, so both resume tasks are still waiting in _acquire_player_lock when the second one arrives. Cancelling the first while it waits is clean: asyncio.Lock drops the cancelled waiter, and get_player_lock's finally only releases the lock and clears _task_held_locks when the lock was actually acquired. The surviving resume reads the group members and queue position when it runs, so remove A then add B (or any other mix) still produces one restart with the final membership. In the normal cmd_set_members path the caller holds the leader lock and lock waiters are served FIFO, so the first resume finishes before a second cmd_set_members can run, and nothing gets cancelled mid-start. Cancelling mid-start only happens when a set_members call skips the leader lock (remove_player cleanup, protocol_linking handover, sync_group leader handover, Player.group/ungroup defaults) or after the 30 s lock timeout. The cancelled restart then exits its lock contexts, play_index's finally resets the transitioning flag, and the replacement re-runs play_media on every current sync client, so playback recovers. create_task's done callback only untracks the entry when it is still the same task, so the replacement stays tracked. prs.summary: Every queue playback start goes through play_index: replace, play, resume, seek, next/previous, transfer_queue, the flow _resume_on_idle and the settle task itself. External sources go through select_source and never start the queue. So the one bump at the top of play_index covers every real start. The replace path swaps the items (load -> update_items, sync) and then calls play_index without yielding (the lock is re-entrant and already held), so the settle loop can't see the new items before the counter moves. ADD and NEXT don't call play_index, so 'items added while idle' still resumes. Autoplay and the dynamic refill still run when nothing started. The task's own refill start bumps expected_starts first, so a refill whose play_index fails after the bump still reaches _finish_queue, same as dev. session_id would not work as the token here: _handle_stop clears it in its finally, which can land after the IDLE report has armed the task, so the task would bail on a legitimate end. The counter is the right choice. Remaining gap: the counter moves at play_index, not when a play action starts. If a user's play_media is still resolving (it holds the playback lock) when the refill fetch returns, the check at playback_tracker.py:568 passes, load() inserts the dynamic tracks, and the task's play_index waits on the lock. After the user's replace has played index 0, it plays next_index (computed against the old list) on the new queue. That is the same symptom, but only when a dynamic-source queue hits the settle fallback and the user starts new media just as the fetch returns.

Like the existing option, the device-level stop leaves the queue session open rather than going through _stop_player_or_its_queue. That is unchanged behaviour.

titles: Description: clarify what it fixes

prs.copilot_note: Changes recommended on 6452f7d05: only the description thread.
prs.summary:
Root cause confirmed: queue pause goes through players._handle_cmd_pause, which resolves _get_control_target(PAUSE, require_active=True) to the active protocol player. Queue _handle_play called queue_player.play() directly, and ProtocolBackedPlayer.play() only forwards to an external source, so LinkPlay (wiim/linkplay_player.py) and UniversalPlayer shells received a no-op. The PR resolves the same target, with a fallback to queue_player.

Paths checked: native player (Sonos, AirPlay native, Cast) has active_output_protocol 'native', so the target is the player itself and behaviour is unchanged. A group or sync_group player has no active output protocol, so the target is None, it falls back to queue_player, and behaviour is unchanged. Universal/LinkPlay with a DLNA, AirPlay or Chromecast protocol now unpauses that protocol player, exactly as the pause did. A protocol without PAUSE never gets here, because pause fell back to stop and the queue is not PAUSED. Sonos with an AirPlay output linked now unpauses the AirPlay protocol that it paused, which is the consistent choice. The wait now targets the protocol player. The parent also updates (on_protocol_player_updated, 0.25 s debounce), so the description's remark that the queue player 'does not change state' is not quite right, but waiting on the protocol is harmless.

Reachability is narrower than the title suggests. The frontend's play button uses players/cmd/play_pause, and players.cmd_play -> _handle_cmd_play already routes a paused player to the control target on dev. Only the player_queues/play and player_queues/play_pause API (for example the Python client's queue_command_play) hit the broken path. It is still a real bug.

DLNA: play() now schedules the same 1 s / 5 s state read-back as skip and seek. For a renderer without events this ends the 5 s wait after about 1 s. For evented renderers it adds two cheap polls.

prs.copilot_note: Changes recommended on 0c2001486: the CRITICAL matches Opus's 60 s window suggestion.
prs.summary:
At the end of a forced_content_length flow stream, _finish_flow_stream now holds the idle connection for (sum of flow_mode_stream_log seconds_streamed - player.corrected_elapsed_time) + 8 s, capped at 180 s, and polls once a second to release early on a new session, a stop (session_id cleared) or shutdown (mass.closing is set at the start of mass.stop). The arithmetic is the same stream-time vs player-position mapping the playback tracker uses for flow mode, so it holds for crossfade and playback speed. Without a position it keeps the old 8 s.

Other players: only flow streams with http profile forced_content_length go through this. That is Bluesound (forced), Chromecast, Yandex Station and Samsung WAM (default 3), plus any player a user switched to profile 3. Sonos, HEOS, DLNA, squeezelite, AirPlay, Sendspin and Snapcast are not affected unless reconfigured. A player that is caught up gets the same 8 s as before. WAM sets no elapsed, so it stays on 8 s. Cast underruns at EOF are already treated as idle via flow_stream_finished, so a longer hold does not keep a Cast group 'playing'. A player that does not drop its buffer on close now goes idle up to 8 s later than before (behind + 8 instead of max(behind, 8)). That costs little.

Layer: the hold-open mechanism was added to core for Bluesound in #5408 and is already gated on profile + queue exhausted. There is no provider hook that owns the HTTP response, and 'hold until the player's reported position reaches what was streamed' is not vendor specific. A provider-level fix would have to add a hook for the same number. The change is in the right place.

Not tested on BluOS hardware. It depends on BluOS 'secs' being cumulative over the flow stream. MA's flow-mode queue tracking for Bluesound already depends on that, so the risk is low.

findings.title: Expired connecting timer is never cleared, so a retry goes idle on its first poll
findings.detail: After 20 s of 'connecting' the method returns IDLE but leaves _connecting_since set. If the user presses play (or a play_media follows) before the next poll, _attr_playback_state is PLAYING again and the next 'connecting' poll sees a timer that is already over 20 s old, so it returns IDLE at once. Simulated on the PR head: polls at 0/10/20 give PLAYING, PLAYING, IDLE, then after an optimistic PLAYING the poll at 20.5 gives IDLE. The old counter behaved the same, but this PR is about slow connects after a command.
findings.fix: Clear the timer on every path that does not return the grace, for example by replacing the else branch with an unconditional `self._connecting_since = None` before the final return (see suggested_fix). Existing tests still pass.

findings.title: Fix depends on play_url answering 'stream'; C700 sequence is unverified
findings.detail: play_media() only sets PLAYING and dynamic polling when play_url() returns 'stream'. If a slow player answers 'connecting', the grace path never runs and the player stays on its previous state at the idle poll interval, so this PR does not change that case. The description gives no log or issue for the NAD C700 behaviour, and GoatsAndMonkeys tests on simulators only.
findings.fix: Ask for a debug log from a slow BluOS player (the play_url response and the following /Status states), as OzGav did on the other PR, before merging.

findings.title: 20 s grace may be too short once #7288's longer lead-out lands
findings.detail: #7288 keeps the flow connection open for as long as the player lags (up to 180 s) plus 8 s. The comment here says the grace spans the streams controller's lead-out. If BluOS reports 'connecting' while it plays out that tail, IDLE after 20 s ends the queue before the sound does, which is what #5408 set out to prevent.
findings.fix: Decide the grace together with #7288. Either confirm on a device that the tail plays out as 'stream', or size MAX_CONNECTING_TIME to the lead-out bound.

suggested_fix.description: Reset the connecting timer whenever the grace is not returned, so a retry after a stuck stream gets a fresh grace.

diff --git a/music_assistant/providers/bluesound/player.py b/music_assistant/providers/bluesound/player.py
index 1ce1ae695c..39ec4851c3 100644
--- a/music_assistant/providers/bluesound/player.py
+++ b/music_assistant/providers/bluesound/player.py
@@ -348,8 +348,7 @@ class BluesoundPlayer(Player):
                 self._connecting_since = time.monotonic()

-        else:
-            self._connecting_since = None
+        self._connecting_since = None

prs.summary: On dev, MAX_CONNECTING_POLLS=2 was sized for the 10 s playback poll (about 20 s), so during the 6 x 0.5 s dynamic polls after a command the third 'connecting' poll returns IDLE after about 1.5 s. Switching to time.monotonic() with a 20 s budget gives the same result at 10 s polls (IDLE on the third poll at t=20) and covers the dynamic window. The trade-off (a stream that never connects shows playing for up to about 20 s) is stated in the description. The grace still spans the 8 s FLOW_STREAM_LEAD_OUT_SECONDS from #5408. Two open points. First, the fix only applies when the player was already PLAYING: play_media() only sets PLAYING and dynamic polling when play_url() answers 'stream'. If a slow player answers 'connecting' to /Play, nothing changes, and no device log shows which one the C700 answers (the 'Set BluOS state to %s' debug line would). Second, _connecting_since is not cleared when the grace runs out. A play()/play_media() before the next poll sets PLAYING optimistically, and the first 'connecting' poll then returns IDLE immediately. I reproduced this in a simulation on the PR head. The old counter had the same flaw, but this PR targets exactly the reconnect-after-command path. Cross-PR note: #7288 (same author, streams lead-out) holds the flow stream up to 180 s and grows the lead-out with player lag. If BluOS reports 'connecting' while it plays out that tail, a fixed 20 s grace would end the queue early again. Review the two together.
